stories.title: Cylinder blast during cooking kills brother and sister:Explosion flattens house; mother and sibling rescued from debris
stories.summary: A gas cylinder exploded while food was being prepared in a Varanasi house on Tuesday morning, around 9. The powerful blast caused the entire house to collapse, killing a brother and sister, while their mother and another brother were trapped under the debris. Police and rescue teams reached the spot promptly, pulled them out, and rushed them to the BHU Trauma Center. Doctors declared two of them dead on arrival. Victims identified The deceased has been identified as, Aman Chaudhary (31) and Preeti alias Lakshmi (24). Four family members were present in the house at the time of the incident. See 3 pictures Location and Impact The incident took place in the Lahartara area, about 7 kilometers from the Kashi Vishwanath Temple. The explosion was so intense that it caused cracks in several nearby houses. Residents rushed out of their homes in panic and gathered to help with rescue efforts. Family background The house belonged to 60-year-old Girija Devi, who lived there with her two sons and a daughter: Their father, Atma Prasad, had passed away three years ago. How the incident happened The house was about 50 years old. While the rear portion had been recently constructed and was still under finishing work, the front portion (around 400 square feet) was in a dilapidated condition. The family was present in this section at the time of the incident. According to initial reports, Girija Devi was cooking when gas began leaking from the cylinder. The pipe caught fire, and before she could react, a massive explosion occurred, causing the house to collapse. Rescue operation After hearing the explosion, neighbors rushed to the scene and informed the police and fire department. With the help of locals, rescue teams pulled all four people from the rubble and sent them to the hospital. Teams from the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) also reached the site. A senior police official confirmed that the explosion was caused by a gas cylinder blast. Eyewitness account Chanda Sahni, a relative living nearby, said: We were asleep when we heard a loud explosion. We rushed outside and saw the house had collapsed. We immediately called others for help and informed the police. The electricity supply was cut off for safety. Investigation underway Authorities are investigating the exact cause of the gas leak and assessing the structural safety of nearby buildings. The incident raises serious concerns about gas safety and the condition of old residential structures.

stories.title: Jaya Prada’s meetings trigger comeback speculation:After talks with BJP state chief and Aparna, questions rise on 2027 elections role
stories.summary: After a long political lull, Jaya Prada has once again sparked speculation about her active return to Uttar Pradesh politics. On March 22, she was in Lucknow, where within a span of just six hours, she met two prominent BJP faces—state president Pankaj Chaudhary and party leader Aparna Yadav. Photos of these meetings quickly surfaced, fueling discussions about whether Jaya Prada is preparing for a larger political role—either within the party organization or as a candidate in the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. Return after long political silence Jaya Prada was last seen in March 2024 in Rampur, when she appeared in an MP-MLA court. Since then, she had largely stayed away from active politics. Her sudden presence among senior BJP leaders has raised eyebrows and triggered speculation about her next move. While she reportedly visited Lucknow to attend a private event, her political engagements during the visit have become the center of attention. Meeting with BJP state chief sparks speculation Jaya Prada began her political career in Andhra Pradesh but gained significant recognition in Uttar Pradesh, particularly from Rampur, where she won the Lok Sabha elections in 2004 and 2009 on a Samajwadi Party (SP) ticket. However, she was expelled from Samajwadi in 2010, after which her political journey saw several shifts—from forming her own outfit to joining the Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD), and eventually the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). After contesting the 2019 Lok Sabha elections from Rampur as a BJP candidate and losing, she remained largely on the sidelines. Her recent meeting with Pankaj Chaudhary has reignited political discussions. According to party insiders, the two leaders have known each other since her tenure as an MP and have met frequently in the past. Following the event, Jaya Prada accompanied Chaudhary to the BJP office, where they reportedly held a long discussion. Although the details of the conversation remain undisclosed, party sources have termed it a routine interaction. However, senior journalist Ravindra Pratap Rana believes otherwise. He suggests that this meeting signals Jaya Prada’s intent to become politically active again. With Chaudhary recently taking charge as state president and working on organizational restructuring, there is speculation that Jaya Prada could be given a significant role within the party. Will she contest from Rampur or elsewhere? Political observers remain divided on whether Jaya Prada will contest the 2027 Assembly elections. After her expulsion from SP, she contested from Bijnor on an RLD ticket, indicating that she does not have an independent vote base in Rampur. Senior journalist Faiz-e-Aam Akbar, who closely tracks Rampur politics, notes that while Jaya Prada is a popular celebrity capable of drawing crowds, her absence from Rampur since her 2019 defeat weakens her prospects in the constituency. Rampur district has five assembly seats—two are currently held by BJP and its ally Apna Dal (S), while three are with Samajwadi. The political landscape has undergone significant changes, especially after Azam Khan was jailed. There is a growing sympathy factor for Azam Khan among sections of the electorate. Reports suggest that his daughter-in-law may contest from the Rampur Sadar seat, making it a tough battleground. The Swar seat is already held by BJP ally Apna Dal (S), while the remaining seats are Muslim-majority constituencies, where Jaya Prada’s candidacy remains uncertain. Given these dynamics, experts believe she may avoid contesting from Rampur to prevent another electoral setback. BJP’s potential counter to Samajwadi’s ‘women card’ Jaya Prada could play a crucial role in BJP’s strategy against the Samajwadi Party’s outreach to women voters. Recently, SP chief Akhilesh Yadav announced an initiative to honor women from different communities and promised an annual financial assistance of ₹40,000 to women if his party comes to power in 2027. The BJP has strongly criticized this move, with Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya raising concerns about women’s safety during SP’s previous tenure. In this context, Jaya Prada could emerge as a strong counter-narrative. During her time in SP, she had a bitter public fallout with Azam Khan, who made controversial remarks about her. BJP may leverage this past conflict to challenge SP’s claims on women empowerment. Meeting With Aparna Yadav Signals Strategic Alignment After her meeting at the BJP office, Jaya Prada visited the residence of Aparna Yadav, who is also the daughter-in-law of Mulayam Singh Yadav. Aparna welcomed her warmly with a traditional tilak, and the two shared a hug—indicating a strong personal rapport. According to sources, they held a closed-door meeting for about an hour. The political significance of this meeting is noteworthy. Both leaders have roots in the Samajwadi Party but are now part of BJP. Their joint presence could be part of a broader strategy to target SP, especially its leadership under Akhilesh Yadav. There is growing speculation that BJP may project both leaders together as influential women faces with SP backgrounds to politically corner Akhilesh. Controversies surrounding Jaya Prada Jaya Prada’s career has also been marked by several controversies: Comeback or Cautious positioning? Jaya Prada’s recent political engagements suggest that she is keen on re-entering active politics. Whether she will contest the 2027 Assembly elections or take up a key organizational role in BJP remains uncertain. However, her meetings with top BJP leaders and her renewed visibility indicate that she could soon play a significant role in the party’s Uttar Pradesh strategy—especially as it prepares for a high-stakes electoral battle in 2027.

stories.title: Rinku Singh appointed Regional Sports Officer:KKR vice-captain misses appointment ceremony; CM Adityanath says, 'He's at training camp'
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Tuesday evening handed over appointment letters to five players in Lucknow and also honoured 40 sportspersons. Cricketer Rinku Singh was among those selected and has been appointed as a Regional Sports Officer (RSO). However, he did not attend the event to collect his letter due to ‘training camp’ in Kolkata. The Chief Minister said Rinku Singh is currently attending a training camp and therefore could not be present. His appointment letter will be handed over later. Meanwhile, Rinku has been appointed as the vice-captain of the Kolkata Knight Riders (KKR) for the IPL 2026. During the ceremony, Yogi Adityanath was also in a light-hearted mood. He joked that even the Home Secretary had once played gilli-danda, adding that wherever a four or six is hit, the bat and ball belong to Uttar Pradesh. Apart from Rinku Singh, Ghazipur’s Rajkumar Pal has been appointed DSP in the police department. Paralympic medallist Praveen Kumar from Noida, along with Ajit Singh from Etawah and Sumiran from Ghaziabad, received appointment letters as Panchayati Raj Officers. Preetipal from Muzaffarnagar has been appointed as a Block Development Officer. : Abhishek, Ishan, Head lead fiery batting, but bowling lacks sting: SRH SWOT Analysis CM Yogi Adityanath hands over appointment letters Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said the players have brought pride to both the country and the state, and honouring them is a matter of pride. He added that the government has allocated ₹200 crore to promote sports, which will help provide better facilities and opportunities to athletes. He also announced that it is time to increase prize money. From next year, the reward amount will be raised to ₹10 lakh, up from the current ₹3.11 lakh. Speaking on the occasion, the Chief Minister highlighted the importance of women and youth in nation-building. He said that during Navratri, the nine forms of Shakti are worshipped, which reflects the tradition of respecting women in society. Quoting, “Yatra Naryastu Pujyante, Tatra Devata Ramante” (where women are honoured, divinity resides), he stressed that empowering women and ensuring their dignity remains a top priority. He added that when youth move forward, they become the foundation of national progress. Both young people and women are excelling in various sports and bringing pride to the country. Rinku Singh appointed KKR's vice-captain Kolkata Knight Riders (KKR) have appointed Rinku Singh as their vice-captain for the IPL 2026 season. The 28-year-old will serve as the deputy to Ajinkya Rahane in the upcoming edition. Rinku replaces Venkatesh Iyer in the leadership role, after the all-rounder was released following a disappointing season, allowing Rinku to step up within the team’s core group. The announcement was made by KKR CEO Venky Mysore during the Knights Unplugged event at Eden Gardens on Tuesday. Rinku remains one of the franchise’s most memorable players, especially after his iconic performance in IPL 2023, where he smashed five consecutive sixes in the final over against Gujarat Titans to secure a stunning victory for KKR. stories.title: Azam in jail, Samajwadi reshuffles Rampur leadership:Party faces backlash prior to 2027 polls as supporters allege betrayal
stories.summary: The political landscape of Rampur is witnessing a significant shift as the Samajwadi Party (SP) attempts to recalibrate its leadership strategy ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. At the center of this transition lies a growing and increasingly visible rift between senior Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan and party chief Akhilesh Yadav. The tension became evident on November 7, 2025, when Akhilesh Yadav visited Rampur to meet Azam Khan shortly after his release from jail. The meeting, which was expected to signal unity, instead revealed underlying discomfort. Azam Khan appeared visibly upset and made remarks that hinted at emotional and political distance. Responding to questions about his relationship with the party leadership, Azam said, “The heart is no longer there; we are working without it. This relationship will take centuries to break. If it gathers rust, I will clean it myself—no one else is needed.” This cryptic yet sharp statement suggested that Azam was wary of external interference in Rampur’s political affairs—particularly any leadership imposed without his consent. Samajwadi Party’s surprise move: Appointment of Surendra Sagar Less than four months later, on March 2, 2026, SP made a decisive move by appointing former BSP leader Surendra Sagar as State Secretary. The decision was taken in Azam Khan’s absence, as he is currently serving a seven-year sentence in a fake PAN card case. The move has sparked resentment among Azam Khan’s loyalists in Rampur. Even weeks after the announcement, discontent continues to simmer on the ground. Supporters argue that the decision reflects a gradual sidelining of Azam, who once single-handedly dominated Rampur’s political landscape. Many believe the timing of the decision is crucial. With Azam Khan barred from contesting elections until at least 2028, the party appears to be preparing for a post-Azam political scenario in Rampur. The big questions The leadership change has raised several important political questions: Strategic reasons behind the shift 1. Strengthening the PDA social coalition The Samajwadi Party has been aggressively promoting its PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak—Backward, Dalit, Minority) formula as a cornerstone of its electoral strategy. By appointing Surendra Sagar, who has strong roots among Dalit communities, SP aims to consolidate its outreach among marginalized sections. Rampur and the broader Moradabad division have a significant Dalit population. Sagar’s induction into a key organizational role sends a message that the party is serious about expanding its social coalition beyond its traditional Muslim-Yadav base. 2. Filling the leadership vacuum Azam Khan’s legal troubles have created a leadership vacuum in Rampur. Having spent nearly 50 months in jail over the past five years, his active participation in politics has been severely limited. After his release in September 2025, Azam Khan remained politically active for just 54 days before being sentenced again in November. This uncertainty has made it difficult for the party to rely solely on him for future electoral battles. By elevating Surendra Sagar, SP is attempting to create an alternative leadership structure that can function independently of Azam’s availability. 3. Targeting BSP’s core vote bank Surendra Sagar’s political background is deeply rooted in the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP). He has served as a district president five times and has a strong network among Dalit and Jatav voters. SP’s strategy appears to be aimed at making inroads into BSP’s traditional vote bank. By bringing in a leader with grassroots connections, the party hopes to attract voters who have historically supported BSP. Sagar’s political journey also reflects shifting alliances in Uttar Pradesh politics. He was expelled from BSP by Mayawati in December 2024, reportedly due to internal disagreements. 4. Managing internal factionalism Rampur’s SP unit has long been plagued by factionalism. Differences between local leaders, including MP Mohibullah Nadvi and Azam Khan’s camp, have created internal friction. By appointing an outsider like Sagar, the party leadership is attempting to neutralize existing power struggles. The move is seen as an effort to balance competing factions and establish a more centralized control over the district unit. From unchallenged authority to political isolation Azam Khan’s political journey in Rampur is nothing short of remarkable. A nine-time MLA and two-time MP, he has been the face of SP in the region for over four decades. His influence peaked during the tenure of Mulayam Singh Yadav. As a cabinet minister, Azam wielded immense power, and his word often carried more weight than official directives. Between 2012 and 2017, it was widely believed that key administrative decisions in Rampur—from the appointment of district officials to local governance matters—were influenced by Azam Khan. One of his most significant achievements was the establishment of Mohammad Ali Jauhar University, which became a symbol of his political clout. However, the political landscape changed dramatically after the rise of Yogi Adityanath in 2017. Since then, Azam has faced multiple legal challenges and prolonged periods of incarceration, significantly reducing his political influence. “SP now wants a silent Azam Khan” Political analyst Tamkeen Fayaz Khan offers a sharp assessment of the current situation. According to him, Azam Khan’s stature within SP remains intact, but his outspoken nature has become a liability for the party. “The party now prefers a silent Azam Khan,” he says. “When he is in jail, he works like a fixed deposit for SP. But when he is out, his statements often create discomfort.” Azam Khan has, on several occasions, publicly questioned the party’s implementation of the PDA formula, particularly its treatment of minority leaders. Such statements have reportedly caused unease within the party leadership. Signs of deliberate distancing There are growing indications that SP may be consciously distancing itself from the Azam Khan family. A notable example was a major minority conference organised in Rampur, where Azam’s son Abdullah Azam Khan was not invited, despite being out on bail at the time. This exclusion was widely interpreted as a signal that the party is no longer prioritizing the Azam family in its political calculations. Both Azam Khan and Abdullah Azam have been disqualified from contesting elections for several years due to legal convictions—further complicating their political future. Ground reactions: Divided opinions Anger among loyalists Many of Azam Khan’s supporters view the leadership change as a betrayal. Local residents argue that his contributions to Rampur’s development—particularly in infrastructure, education, and healthcare—are unmatched. One resident remarked that even top leaders would struggle to match Azam’s influence in Rampur. Support for change At the same time, there is a section of voters that welcomes the shift. They believe that Rampur’s politics has been dominated by a single family for too long. Supporters of Surendra Sagar argue that his grassroots approach and focus on village-level outreach could bring a new dimension to local politics. Experts: Azam Khan still a dominant force Despite the current developments, many political observers believe that Azam Khan’s influence in Rampur remains formidable. His legacy, built over decades, continues to command respect among large sections of the population. Senior journalists and analysts argue that replacing a leader of his stature is not an easy task. While Surendra Sagar may strengthen the party organizationally, matching Azam’s mass appeal will be a significant challenge. Conclusion: A high-stakes political gamble The Samajwadi Party’s decision to promote Surendra Sagar marks a clear shift in its political strategy. By attempting to diversify its leadership and expand its social base, the party is preparing for a future where it cannot rely solely on Azam Khan. However, this transition comes with risks. Alienating Azam’s loyal support base could weaken the party’s position in Rampur—a constituency that has long been considered its stronghold. As the 2027 elections approach, Rampur is set to become a key battleground, reflecting not just electoral dynamics but also the evolving power equations within the Samajwadi Party.

stories.title: Digvijaya Singh visits Ram Temple in Ayodhya for first time:Congress leader says, 'Faith must not be used for politics'
stories.summary: Former MP CM and Congress Rajya Sabha MP Digvijaya Singh visited Ayodhya for the first time today, Thursday, to have darshan of Ram Lalla. Congress workers welcomed him at Ayodhya's International Airport. After that, he went to meet former Uttar Pradesh Congress President Nirmal Khatri at his residence. This is the first time Digvijaya Singh has visited Ayodhya and had darshan of Ram Lalla after the construction of the Ram Temple and the Pran Pratishtha ceremony. We do not use religion for business politics: Digvijaya Singh After having darshan of Ram Lalla in Ayodhya, Digvijaya Singh said, “In Congress, every person follows religion according to their faith. We do not misuse religion for business nor for politics.” "No matter what religion a person belongs to, be it Hindu, Muslim, Sikh, Parsi, or Christian, every person practices their religion according to their faith. But it should not be politically misused. Religion should not be misused for business as well," he added. Regarding the Iran-Israel war, Digvijaya Singh said, “Everyone is seeing the crowds at cooking gas stations and petrol pumps. When the Lord calls, every person comes. Also, it is not possible that you come to Lord Ram's abode and do not visit Hanuman Ji.” Digvijaya went to ask for a Rajya Sabha seat: BJP On Digvijaya Singh's visit to Ayodhya to see Ramlala, BJP's state media in-charge Ashish Agrawal said, “Digvijaya Singh is making various efforts after losing his Rajya Sabha seat. stories.title: Weather to remain disturbed in UP for 5 days:Rain and hail alert, winds up to 50 kmph; know where it will rain today
stories.summary: The weather in Uttar Pradesh is likely to stay unsettled for the next five days, with rain and strong winds expected in many areas. The Meteorological Department has issued a rain alert for the western parts of the state today. Cloud movement will continue on Thursday in districts such as Bareilly, Agra and Mathura. Some places may see light drizzle during the day, while winds could reach speeds of up to 50 kmph. According to the Meteorological Department, the change in weather is due to the impact of a Western Disturbance. The spell of storms and rain that began last week is expected to continue till the end of March, with chances of thunder, lightning and even hailstorms in some areas. However, no rainfall was recorded anywhere in the state in the last 24 hours. As a result, temperatures rose by up to 5°C. Prayagraj was the hottest place with a maximum temperature of 35.6°C, while the lowest temperature was recorded in Bijnor at 14.5°C. Lucknow's meteorologist, Atul Kumar Singh, said- Two western disturbances are becoming active in the state. Light rain will begin in Western UP from today. Gradually, its effect will reach Eastern UP. The second disturbance will become active on March 29. This will bring good rain across the entire state. Wind will blow at a speed of 40-50 (kmph). There will be a drop of 4C to 5C in temperature. A feeling of cold will be experienced. See 3 pictures of the weather Weather conditions in Western UP Why the fluctuations in the weather? The Meteorological Department says that the weather in the mountains of Uttarakhand is constantly changing. A rain and snowfall alert has been issued for the next 2 to 3 days. Its direct effect will be seen in UP. Cold winds coming from the mountains will make one feel cold. Damage to wheat and pigeon pea crops due to the storm, and how to protect them Agricultural experts say that rain and strong winds will affect Rabi, Zaid, and horticultural crops. At this time, pods are forming in pigeon pea, mustard, gram, peas, moong, and groundnut. Grains are filling. Strong winds can cause pods to burst and grains to fall off. Wheat crops can also fall due to strong winds, which poses a risk of reduced yield. In vegetables, flowers, and small fruits of okra, tomato, bottle gourd, cucumber, watermelon, muskmelon, brinjal, and chilli can fall off. Farmers have been advised to immediately harvest the ripened crop and store it in a safe place. Do not allow water to accumulate in the fields; arrange for proper drainage for this. The government said - If crops fall, farmers can claim insurance Amidst the recent rain and hailstorms and the upcoming alert, there is good news for farmers whose crops have been damaged. According to the government, if crops are damaged within 14 days of harvesting, farmers can claim insurance under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana. The district administration will survey crop damage due to natural calamities and submit a report, based on which the UP government may decide to provide compensation.

stories.title: Congress Rajya Sabha MP Digvijaya Singh visits Ram Lalla:Offers prayers at Hanumangarhi, says he came after receiving divine call
stories.summary: Congress Rajya Sabha MP and former Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh, Digvijaya Singh, arrived in Ayodhya on Thursday morning. First, he offered prayers at the Hanumangarhi temple. After that, he visited Ram Lalla and then went to Kanak Bhawan to seek blessings. During this, Congress leaders and workers were also present. Speaking to the media, Digvijaya Singh said - When the Lord calls, everyone comes. So when I received the call, I came. It felt good to have darshan of the Lord. I also contributed to becoming Ram Kanak Bhawan belongs to the Maharaja of Tikamgarh, Madhya Pradesh, and I also went there to seek blessings. He had a long-standing wish to have a darshan of Ramlala. I also made a small contribution to the construction of the Ram Temple. The Lord called, and we came. In Congress, every person practices religion according to their faith. We do not misuse religion for business or for politics. When asked about the development of Ayodhya, he said - A one or two-hour journey doesn't reveal much; the people of Ayodhya know what the impact will be. Meanwhile, on the fuel and gas shortage in the country, Digvijaya Singh said - under BJP rule, not only are there queues. People are becoming poorer and poorer. Some people are becoming richer and richer. Congress workers welcomed him at the airport This was Digvijaya Singh's first visit to Ayodhya after the construction of the Ram Temple and the consecration ceremony. He arrived at Maharishi Valmiki International Airport around 9 AM, where Congress workers gave him a grand welcome. After this, he visited the residence of former UP Congress state president Nirmal Khatri to inquire about his well-being. After this, Digvijaya Singh left to visit and offer prayers at Hanumangarhi, Ramlala, and Kanak Bhawan. After completing the darshan and prayers, he departed for Lucknow. Digvijaya Singh said - I have not come to do politics On the opposition to the Ram Janmabhoomi temple, Digvijaya Singh said - I have never opposed the construction of the Ram temple. May Lord Shri Ram's blessings be upon everyone. Meanwhile, a press release issued by Digvijaya Singh's office stated that he is a descendant of Saint Pipaji Maharaj of the Ramanandi sect. In his ancestral home, Raghogarh, ancient temples of Raghuji Maharaj (Lord Ram) and Hanumanji are also located. On January 18, 2021, he donated Rs 1,11,111 to the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust for the construction of the Ram Temple. It also mentioned his 3,300-kilometre-long Narmada Parikrama, which he completed on foot, describing him as connected to the Sanatan tradition.

stories.title: ‘Ravi Kishan would be in Dubai if no war’:CM Yogi takes a jibe, assures gas cylinders will be delivered as before
stories.summary: In Gorakhpur, CM Yogi said that there is a war going on in the Middle East. If it drags on, it will affect every person. We should not panic. Do not pay attention to rumors. When a challenge comes, everyone has to walk hand in hand with the government. This is true patriotism. Yogi also took a dig at MP Ravi Kishan. He said that if there was no war in the Middle East, Ravi Kishan would have been in Dubai. But, since the situation there is not good, he thought, "Let me also go to Sahjanwa." He further said that Ravi Kishan was not believing it. He was saying that 5000 crore rupees must have been spent on the development of Gorakhpur. I said, "No, you are wrong. More than one lakh crore rupees have been spent in Gorakhpur alone in the last 9-10 years." Regarding the queues for cylinders, he said that if the government has taken any step in the interest of the country, we have to prepare ourselves for it. No one should go to get a cooking gas cylinder before it is finished. Just as cylinders used to reach homes before, they will be delivered now as well. There is no need to stand in line. Yogi said that some people are trying to create disorder. Go to get diesel and petrol only when necessary. If you form a queue, people will doubt our patriotism. He also said that Earlier, CM Yogi inaugurated the IT Park built in the Gorakhpur Industrial Development Authority (GIDA). The park is built on 3.5 acres of land in Sector 7, near the GIDA office. stories.title: Noida International Airport to become NCR’s new global gateway:Built at cost of ₹11,200 crore, PM Modi to inaugurate on March 28
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate the Noida International Airport in Jewar, Gautam Buddh Nagar, on March 28. He will visit the terminal at around 11:30 am and formally open Phase-1 of the airport at 12 pm. He will also address a public gathering during the event. The Noida International Airport, also known as Jewar Airport, is one of the largest new airports being built in India. It has been developed under a public-private partnership model with an investment of about ₹11,200 crore. This will be the second major international airport serving the Delhi-NCR region, alongside the Indira Gandhi International Airport. The new airport is expected to boost connectivity and help turn NCR into a major global aviation hub. Key Features of the Airport Designed as a Multi-Modal Transport Hub The airport has been designed as a multi-modal transport hub, ensuring easy integration of road, rail, metro, and regional transit systems. Located along the Yamuna Expressway, this airport will ensure excellent connectivity for both passengers and cargo. Direct and Fast Connectivity from Delhi-NCR To give new momentum to traffic in Noida, a 1.8 km-long elevated road is being built from Chilla Road to Sector-94. For this, the Noida Authority has approved a budget of 150 crore rupees. This route will provide direct access from Delhi to Noida International Airport and will provide permanent relief from heavy traffic jams in Sector-18 and Film City. The inauguration of Noida International Airport is considered a significant step that will take India's aviation infrastructure to new heights. This project will not only reduce congestion in the NCR but also boost regional and international connectivity.

stories.title: Akhilesh mocks govt over gas crisis, says he got clay-stoves:On his party leader Pooja Pal's removal, SP chief claims she was 'misled'
stories.summary: SP chief Akhilesh Yadav took a jibe at CM Yogi during a press conference at 12 noon on Thursday in Lucknow. He said - he is even more shrewd than the shrewd. They misled our MLA (Pooja Pal). Tell us, where should we file the FIR. He said - She was a woman, that's why she wasn't removed earlier. Later she had to be removed out of compulsion. These statements are being made so that she gets a ticket from somewhere. Actually, on March 24, Pooja Pal had said that CM Yogi is a shrewd chief minister. He ended mafias like Atiq and Mukhtar Ansari. Akhilesh also questioned the CM's English tweet. He said- He didn't write this tweet himself, rather it was done through AI, whose lie has been caught. Those who don't know the full form of AI, how will they understand PDA. How will they understand the pain and suffering of PDA. The SP chief also raised questions about the MOUs signed by the government. He said that the MOUs have no financial basis. All MOUs should be investigated. Regarding the gas shortage, he said - We have built two clay stoves. Read Akhilesh Yadav's key points 1- As the pain increases, the PDA will keep growing Akhilesh said - Don't fall for CM's words, he is not a Yogi. He can say anything. It's time to move on. We hear that a movie 'Ganja Ganj' is being made. As the pain increases, the PDA will keep growing. Therefore, we Samajwadi people are moving forward by uniting them to bring respect to PDA. 2- BJP government's MoUs should be investigated Akhilesh said that many MoUs signed during BJP government have no financial basis. We demand that all MoUs signed so far should be investigated. These were done to mislead the public. He said - The government is also spreading confusion in the name of AI. There's talk about a company that was formed in 2025 and its website was created in 2026. The whole matter came to light just from the 5% incentive. 3- 'Everyone in BJP is a Propaganda Minister' Attacking BJP sharply, Akhilesh said that during Hitler's time there was one propaganda minister, but in the BJP government all ministers at the center and state are propaganda ministers. Everyone thinks of themselves as the Prime Minister. He said- BJP is the first political party in the world that spends billions of rupees to tarnish others' image. He said- The sofa they are breaking in Lok Bhavan, who got it made? Who got Lok Bhavan built? 4- 'BJP only made people stand in lines' Taking a jibe at inflation and gas cylinders, Akhilesh said that a new month is coming, what did people get in BJP government except standing in lines? People make budgets planning to refill cylinders at month end. He alleged that the government reduced 14.2 kg cylinder to 10 kg. We have made two clay stoves at our home. We have arranged to cook food with wood and coal at our place. If there is difficulty for one more month, everyone will have to do the same. Small traders who used to sell chaat, samosa, momos etc. on gas are facing the most trouble. 5- Asked about dress code in Parliament - Should we wear shorts Akhilesh commented on Parliament dress code - Should we wear shorts? He himself has stopped wearing shorts and wears pants. If all BJP people come wearing shorts, we will also come wearing them. 6- Announcement of Emperor Ashoka's statue Akhilesh announced that Emperor Ashoka's statue will be installed on a golden throne at the River Front in Lucknow.

stories.title: 'Monalisa trapped in the net of jihadis':Director Sanoj Mishra rubbishes allegations of inappropriate touching of Mahakumbh girl, who married with a Muslim
stories.summary: Film director Sanoj Mishra spoke publicly for the first time after Monalisa Bhonsle made allegations against him. In a video released on Wednesday, he said his determination to make ordinary things special “burned my own hands,” but he added he does not regret trying sincerely. He claimed that Monalisa is “trapped in the net of jihadis” and is being trained to make false accusations. He said her entire family, including her mother, sister, father Jai Singh, and other Sanatani people, support him. Fight against Love-Jihad will continue- Sanoj Mishra added that his fight against what he called Love-Jihad will continue. He also said this is not the first time his character has been questioned, and every time, the truth has come out. On Tuesday, Monalisa Bhonsle accused Mishra of touching her inappropriately during the shooting of the film The Diary of Manipur. At a press conference in Kochi, Kerala, she said he touched her ten times and called him “not a good person.” She also said her family did not support her, and she questioned whether facing such harassment is expected from newcomers in the film industry. Monali had sought security from the Central, Kerala, and Madhya Pradesh governments Monali had sought help from the Central government along with the Kerala and Madhya Pradesh governments. She had said that she and her husband Farman are receiving death threats. Her posters are being burnt. The director is spreading false information about her. She does not want to work with such a person. Monalisa said - If separated from husband, both will commit suicide Monalisa said - False accusations regarding the marriage should not be made against her husband. Both got married in a temple according to Hindu rituals. The director is calling their marriage 'love jihad'. He is trying to spread tension in society. If an attempt is made to separate her from her husband, both will commit suicide. Farman said - The director is calling him a terrorist Farman also alleged that the director is calling him a terrorist. Accusations are being made against him because he was born into a Muslim family and his name is Farman Khan. He believes in Sree Narayana Guru. They got married in one of his temples. Sanoj said - Kerala's Christian missionary is conducting a joint operation with jihadists 24 hours after Monalisa's allegations, Sanoj Mishra released a video on Wednesday to clarify. He said - For the past several days, Monalisa's love jihad matter has been ongoing. After that, I started a campaign against love jihad with the victim's family. This was widely praised across the country, but now the matter is changing. Along with jihadists, Kerala's Christian missionary is also conducting a joint operation against me. That girl is being persuaded and made to say baseless things on social media. 'I will not bow my head before jihadists' He said - Today I am feeling the pain of that father, for whom Monalisa said that she fears for her life from that man. All this has been happening since the launch of my film's trailer, but I will not bow my head before jihadists. In the coming time, a major accident might happen to me or my family, which is why I have come before you through this video. 'Something untoward might happen to me' He said that he would need everyone's support. My mother is very ill. Your support will become my strength. The entire episode has been fabricated to defame Sanatan Dharma and portray Hindu-Muslim marriages as successful, but the public knows that all this is wrong. Monalisa's father said - Never complained Meanwhile, in a conversation with Dainik Bhaskar, Monalisa's father, Jaisingh Bhonsle, also called the allegations false. He said that during the shooting, he and his family were with Monalisa 24 hours a day. Sanoj Mishra considers her like his own daughter. Sanoj is helping us, which is why he is being targeted. He appealed to his daughter that she should not make false allegations under anyone's pressure.

stories.title: Body of child hidden in container, covered with flour sack:Throat slit in Agra, remains found in tenant’s room, mother faints; police hunt suspect
stories.summary: An 8-year-old girl, daughter of a shoe trader, was found murdered with her throat slit in Agra. Her body was discovered on Wednesday night around 8 PM inside a metal container kept in a tenant’s room. The container had been filled with flour on top to conceal the body. The child had gone missing on Tuesday afternoon while playing outside her home. Her body was recovered nearly 30 hours later. Upon seeing her daughter’s body, the mother fainted. The incident created tension in the area, with residents taking to the streets in protest. Tenant absconding, primary suspect Police suspect the tenant, identified as Sunil, who worked as a painter and lived in a rented room above the factory owned by the girl’s father. He has been missing since the incident and is believed to be the main accused. According to police, a case of kidnapping and murder has been registered against him, and 10 teams have been deployed to trace him. See 3 pictures related to the incident How the child went missing The victim’s father said the girl left home around 2 PM on Tuesday to play with neighborhood children. When she did not return by evening, the family initially assumed she had gone for tuition. However, when she failed to return by 4:30 PM, concern grew, and a search was launched. Police were informed, and CCTV footage from the area was examined. The girl was last seen buying chips from a nearby shop before heading back toward her home. Search operation and Rising suspicion Police formed four teams: Initially, no clue was found. The father later informed police that the tenant had been helping in the search and had even accompanied him to the police station to file a missing complaint. However, suspicion arose when the tenant suddenly disappeared after locking his room. Body recovered from tenant’s room Acting on suspicion, police broke open the tenant’s locked room on Wednesday night. Inside, they found the girl’s body stuffed inside a flour container. A sack of flour and a red quilt had been placed over it to hide the body. Public outrage and Road blockade As police attempted to take the body for postmortem, family members and locals protested, demanding the arrest of the accused first. The situation escalated into a road blockade on Fatehabad Road, with stone-pelting and attempts to vandalize vehicles. The protest continued for about 30 minutes before police officials, including DCP City Syed Ali Abbas, intervened and calmed the crowd, assuring swift action. Postmortem findings The postmortem, conducted on Thursday morning by a panel of three doctors, revealed: The body was handed over to the family and buried around 9:30 AM. Family demands strict action The victim’s aunt demanded the harshest punishment for the accused, even calling for an encounter. Police have assured that the case will be taken to a fast-track court and strict action will be ensured.

stories.title: Rush at petrol pumps in UP, Gorakhpur DM steps in:Police deployed in Gonda and Prayagraj; officials assure stock available for 22 days in state
stories.summary: Rumours about petrol and diesel shortage spread across several districts in Uttar Pradesh, leading to panic buying on Wednesday night. Large crowds gathered at petrol pumps in Gorakhpur, Gonda, Deoria and Maharajganj, with many people bringing big containers to stock fuel. Long queues were seen at several places, where people waited for hours. In Prayagraj and Gonda, police had to step in at petrol pumps to control the situation, after which fuel was supplied to people. Oil companies have a 22-day stock. So, do not pay attention to rumors. There is no need to panic and buy or hoard excessive fuel - Sanjay Bhandari, coordinator for oil companies In Gorakhpur, due to the rumors, DM Deepak Meena and SSP Dr. Kaustubh came out on the streets late at night. They visited pumps and appealed to people not to fall for rumors. People should take diesel and petrol as they do on normal days. There is no need to stand in long queues. There was a huge crowd at petrol pumps in Gonda late into the night. Farmers were seen standing in long queues to get diesel. Farmers fear that if diesel runs out, they will face difficulties in threshing wheat in the coming days. About 13,168 petrol pumps are operating in the state. Pump owners say that the crowd suddenly increased by 3 to 4 times. They didn't even understand why the crowd suddenly increased, even though there was sufficient oil. See 3 pictures

stories.title: IPS officer hits back at body shamers:Says she will deal with trolls; many who commented had no photos on profiles
stories.summary: Mirzapur SP Aparna Rajat Kaushik has come into the spotlight after facing heavy trolling on social media. A video of her press briefing received thousands of body-shaming and offensive comments, raising serious concerns. The situation became so serious that the police social media team had to disable the comment section. Speaking on the issue, IPS Aparna Kaushik said that harassment in public places has largely reduced, but such behaviour has now shifted online. She added that strict action will be taken to deal with this problem as well. Read the full interview verbatim Question: What was your reaction after reading comments on Instagram for the first time? Aparna- When the comments started coming in, I watched them for 15 to 20 minutes. The people who were commenting hadn't even put their photos on their IDs. I thought, why should I waste my energy on people who don't have confidence in themselves? I have bigger things to do. Question- What did you do after seeing the comments? Aparna- I look at everything like a police officer. When the police team analyzed the data, most of them turned out to be fake accounts. It will take some time to find out about them. As a police officer, I have to set priorities: we listen to people's problems first, then our own. Question- How do you feel as a woman after seeing vulgar comments? Aparna- It's not that this only happens to women; many men also face such behavior. Comments are made on their appearance. Often, people prefer to engage in negative things. After you've made a comment, you should think, "Did I become a good person by doing this?" Ask anyone who made a comment what they contributed? They won't be able to give any answer. Question- Has people's mindset towards women not changed yet? Aparna- You know, abuses are always female-centric. Whenever I go to schools, I tell the boys, "Who are you pointing out when you use those abuses? You also have a mother, a sister at home." This becomes a 'part of the psyche'. You start looking at females through the same lens. We will have to stop these things. We tell them that females are inferior, and they are superior. If you look today, many girls are board toppers, they top exams. Question- Is there a need for big action on social media comments? Aparna- Look, earlier eve-teasing or harassment used to happen in physical spaces. Gradually, this has shifted to online spaces. As society is evolving, the pattern of crime has also changed. We are training our team to deal with this. There's another thing, there are also people among them who only have 2 followers. We should not spend our energy on such people. Question- Some IDs are no longer visible after commenting on your post? Aparna- You are right. I myself saw that as quickly as they commented, they also ran away with their tails between their legs. If you do something wrong, it's obvious that you will have fear. Whatever wrong you do, whether in physical space or social space, action will be taken. Question- Will an attempt be made to set a precedent by taking action? Aparna- Look, you cannot erase activity on social media. Its digital footprint always remains. Therefore, it is important to teach such people a lesson. If you upload reels of traffic violations, or reels doing something wrong, and it comes to our attention, action will definitely be taken. Question - Do you consider joining the civil service a success? Aparna - I am not naming that district, just telling the case. There was a widow woman between 55-60 years old. Her neighbor tried to grab her when he found her alone. Now think, she lives alone, she is a widow, what must she have felt? As soon as we received the complaint, the investigation officer worked very intelligently. We filed the charge sheet within 3 days. We strongly put the case on trial. We expedited its trial. When the verdict came in the case, the accused was punished. After this, the woman came to my office with a box of sweets to meet me. Seeing that, I became very emotional. She also became emotional. There are many cases, but sometimes when you bring full justice to its conclusion, it's a very sweet victory. In many cases, the case proceeds after the accused is caught. Sometimes we get transferred, and we don't get to see the victim receive justice. But, that time I was lucky. It is necessary that you don't stay silent, call out boldly.

stories.title: Row erupts over BJP’s new district executive appointments:Attempt-to-murder accused gets general secretary post, teacher gets media charge
stories.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in Uttar Pradesh has come under scrutiny after announcing its district executive committees, which were finalized after significant delays and internal deliberations. Initially scheduled to be completed by March 2, the process took an additional 19 days, with committees being announced on March 21. Despite the delay, district units in Gorakhpur region—considered the stronghold of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath—are yet to be formed. Despite extensive deliberations, the newly announced executive has quickly become mired in controversy. A shocking case has emerged from Ayodhya, where an accused in an attempt-to-murder case has been appointed as General Secretary—he is reportedly among the district’s top-10 criminals. In Lucknow, a government school teacher has been made the BJP’s media in-charge, a move that appears to violate the service rules of the education department. In Uttar Pradesh, the BJP has reorganised its structure into 98 districts, with district executives formed in each. However, the mandated inclusion of at least seven women in every executive has largely been ignored. Lalitpur remains the only district where this requirement has been fulfilled. Read this special report… Attempt-to-murder accused appointed in Ayodhya A major controversy has emerged from Ayodhya, where Shivendra Singh has been appointed as district general secretary. According to police records, Singh faces multiple cases, including attempted murder and assault. He is also listed among the top 10 criminals in the erstwhile Faizabad district. Sources claim Singh is a close associate of rebel Samajwadi Party MLA Abhay Singh. Party insiders say objections were raised by senior leaders from district to national levels, but he was appointed under pressure from a senior state-level functionary. Ayodhya city president Kamlesh Srivastava defended the decision, stating that “registration of a case does not make someone a criminal” and that investigations are ongoing. Government teacher appointed media in-charge in Lucknow In Lucknow, the party appointed Chintamani Pandey as district media in-charge, sparking another controversy. Pandey is currently serving as an assistant teacher at a primary school in Haidergarh, Barabanki. As per education department service rules, government employees are prohibited from holding positions in political parties. Pandey had previously been suspended during the 2022 Assembly elections for allegedly campaigning for BJP candidate Shalabh Mani Tripathi. Responding to the controversy, Pandey argued that council teachers are neither central nor state government employees and cited a Supreme Court observation describing teachers as “gurus.” However, Basic Education Officer Naveen Kumar Pathak clarified that such an appointment violates service rules and is not permissible. Women’s representation norms ignored The BJP has divided Uttar Pradesh into 98 organizational districts, each with a district executive committee. As per party guidelines, each committee must include at least seven women. However, except for Lalitpur, no district has fulfilled this requirement. Similarly, the rule mandating 30 women members in district executive bodies has largely been ignored. Irregularities in social representation The party had also mandated representation for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Other Backward Classes based on local demographics. Sources allege that in some districts, surnames of office bearers were deliberately omitted to project them as belonging to OBC or Dalit communities. Age criteria overlooked State BJP president Pankaj Chaudhary had directed that office bearers should be between 30 and 50 years of age, with relaxations for women and SC/ST candidates. Despite this, several districts have appointed individuals aged between 60 and 65, violating the prescribed norms. Leaders from other parties dominate According to party sources, recommendations from MLAs were given significant weight in forming district committees, leading to alleged sidelining of grassroots workers. More than 30% of BJP MLAs in the state are said to have joined from other parties. Their influence has reportedly resulted in their loyalists being appointed to key district positions, leaving long-time cadre members dissatisfied. In Sarojini Nagar, supporters of MLA Rajeshwar Singh are reportedly unhappy after names recommended by him were excluded, while his opponents were accommodated. Formation timeline and Current status As per the guidelines issued by state president Pankaj Chaudhary, district committees were to be finalized by March 2. However, due to delays, announcements were made between March 20 and 21. So far, committees in over 65 districts across regions like Kashi, Braj, West, Awadh, and Kanpur have been declared, while the Gorakhpur region remains pending.

stories.title: Lucknow BJP's new district working committee announced:New and old faces included, focus on strengthening booth-level organisation
stories.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party has announced the new executive committee of the Lucknow district unit. After the recommendation of state president Pankaj Chaudhary, district president Vijay Maurya announced the entire team. It includes 8 vice presidents, 3 general secretaries, 8 ministers, 1 treasurer, and 3 joint treasurers. A total of 35 officials were given responsibilities, including media and IT in-charges. The announced executive committee has taken into account organisational balance and regional representation. Under the Awadh region, this team of Lucknow district includes both experienced faces and new workers. This team has been prepared keeping in view the upcoming elections and organisational expansion, so that strength can be brought up to the booth level. Responsibilities fixed from Vice President to General Secretary In the new team, Rajkumar Verma, Arvind Yadav, Krishna Kant Awasthi, Hansraj Lodhi, Anil Singh Chauhan, Shiv Darshan Yadav, Pratima Verma and Hansraj Rawat have been given responsibility as district vice presidents. While Dhirendra Pandey "Dhiru", Ankit Gupta and Gaurav Singh Chauhan have been appointed as district general secretaries. These positions are considered to have an important role in the organisation's operations. District Minister and Treasurer positions also appointed Raju Kashyap, Dhirendra Maurya "Dhiru", Vivek Singh, Sanjeev Mishra, Mukesh Sharma, Shyampyari Lodhi, Pratima Singh and Kamta Prasad Rawat have been included in the District Minister position. Chandra Prakash Awasthi (Advocate) has been made District Treasurer, and Abhishek Rajput, Gyanendra Singh Pappan and Amit Tiwari have been made Co-Treasurers. Media, Social Media and IT Team also announced BJP has set separate responsibilities, keeping in mind the media and digital platforms. Chitranmani Pandey has been made District Media In-charge, while Santosh Sharma and Ashish Kanaujia have been given the responsibility of Co-Media In-charge. In social media, Ravi Dwivedi has been made coordinator and Ajit Yadav and Nirmal Singh have been made co-coordinators. In the IT cell, Rajkumar Rohit has been given the responsibility of coordinator, and Vipin Saxena and Amit Kashyap have been made co-coordinators. Goal to strengthen the organization at grassroots level District President Vijay Maurya said that the objective of the new executive committee is to make the organisation active and strong up to the booth level. Clear instructions have been given to all office bearers to remain active in their respective areas and ensure government schemes reach every person. He expressed confidence that with the new team, BJP will become organizationally stronger in Lucknow and will firmly face the upcoming political challenges.

stories.title: Govt employee leaks fighter jet locations to Pakistan:In touch with ISI since 2023; shared Air Force, military base details
stories.summary: Rajasthan’s Intelligence team has arrested a government employee from Chabua Air Force Station in Assam on charges of espionage. The accused was allegedly passing sensitive information related to the Indian Air Force to Pakistani handlers. He had shared confidential details, including locations of fighter aircraft, missile systems, and information related to officers and personnel. ADG (Intelligence) Prafull Kumar said the case began in January 2026 with the arrest of Jhabraram, a resident of Jaisalmer. During interrogation, the name of another suspect, Sumit Kumar, surfaced, who was in continuous contact with Pakistani intelligence agencies. Sent confidential information to Pakistani handlers Investigations revealed that the accused, Sumit Kumar (36), son of Beni Madhav, is a resident of Lahurpar in Prayagraj district (Uttar Pradesh). He is currently posted as an MTS (Multi Tasking Staff) at Chabua Air Force Station in Dibrugarh, Assam. Misusing his position, he collected confidential information related to the Air Force station and passed it to Pakistani handlers through social media. Was in contact with Pakistani intelligence agency since 2023 The Rajasthan Intelligence team, in coordination with Air Force Intelligence in New Delhi, detained Sumit Kumar from Chabua. He was then brought to the Central Interrogation Centre in Jaipur, where multiple intelligence agencies questioned him. During interrogation, it was revealed that the accused had been in contact with a Pakistani intelligence agency since 2023 and was sharing sensitive information in exchange for money. The probe found that apart from Chabua Air Force Station, he had also shared crucial information related to Nal Air Force Station in Bikaner and other military bases. This included locations of fighter aircraft, missile systems and confidential details related to officers and staff. Additionally, the accused used mobile numbers issued in his name to create social media accounts for Pakistani handlers.

stories.title: 4 die, including woman and child, in Sambhal road accident:Car hits tempo while overtaking, vehicle crushed to half size
stories.summary: On Sunday evening, a speeding car and a tempo collided. In the accident, 4 people, including a woman, died, while 9 people were injured. Among them, 5 are in critical condition in Sambhal. The accident occurred near Udharanpur village in the Dhanari area on the Agra-Moradabad National Highway. The collision was so severe that both the tempo and the car were badly damaged. The tempo's body was crushed to half its size. Upon receiving information about the accident, the police and the 108 ambulance reached the spot. The injured were immediately taken to Community Health Center (CHC) Bahjoi. 12 people, including women and children, were sitting in the tempo According to police, the Ertiga car was moving at high speed. It was going from the district headquarters, Bahajoi, towards Barwala, while the tempo was coming towards Bahajoi. During this time, the car driver tried to overtake another vehicle, due to which it lost control and collided with the tempo. The tempo had 12 people on board, including children and women. There were two people in the car, including the driver. In the accident, Rajesh, son of Kallu (20) from Pathakpur ki Madaiya of Bahajoi police station, Rajni (14), daughter of Ompal from Raipur Kala, and Kishori (40 years), son of Jhandu Singh from Manakpur of Dhanari police station, died. One woman's identity has not yet been established. Rajni's father, Ompal (35), mother, Pravesh (32), sister, Saloni (7), and brother, Kuldeep (2) are undergoing treatment. Shaukin (32), son of Rafi from Akbarpur Bahjai, Rajnish (20), son of Kallu from Pathakpur ki Madhaiya, who were in the tempo, and car passengers Priyanchu (14), son of Ramgopal, and Kripal (35), son of Puran Singh from Lahra Nagla Shyam village of Junawai police station, are admitted to the hospital. Rajni's mother, Pravesh, said that she lives in Delhi with her husband Ompal and supports the family by selling golgappas and vegetables from a street cart. She said that they were returning home from Delhi and were about to reach the village by tempo. Just 10 minutes away from home, a vehicle crashed hard into their tempo, causing this accident. Meanwhile, Rajesh's father, Kallu, said that his son had left home alone to take a bath in the Rajghat Ganga, but he boarded the tempo with other passengers. He said that Rajesh was to be married in a month. Kallu said, "He was my only son," and broke down while saying this. CCTV investigation will reveal cause of accident CO Bahajoi Dr. Pradeep Kumar said, CCTV cameras installed in the surrounding area are being examined to determine the causes of the accident. 10 seriously injured people have been referred to the district hospital for better treatment. 4 people including a woman and a young girl have died in this accident. All bodies have been sent for post-mortem.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:Iran claims 'enemy' F-15 jet shot down near Hormuz; CM Yogi distributes nursing appointment letters to 1,100 women more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. Iran claims 'enemy' F-15 jet shot down near Hormuz On the 23rd day of the US-Israel-Iran war, Iran has stated that its air defence system targeted an enemy F-15 fighter jet near the Strait of Hormuz. According to Iran’s consulate in Mumbai, the aircraft had entered Iranian airspace near the country’s southern coast, after which it was intercepted and targeted with a surface-to-air missile. 2. CM Yogi distributes nursing appointment letters to 1,100 women: Dy CM Pathak targets opponents, says era of job loot is over Yogi Adityanath distributes joining letters to 1,097 female and 131 male nursing officers in Lucknow on Sunday, saying at a program held at Lok Bhawan that receiving appointment letters during Navratri reflects the growing strength of women. 3. New claims in Farsa Baba death case: Disciples allege truck ran him over intentionally; questions raised over police hiding the container Whether the death of Farsa Wale Baba aka Chandrashekhar Singh (45) in Mathura is an accident or murder... this mystery is getting more complicated. Baba's supporters are calling it murder, while police are saying it was an accident. According to the theory stated by the police, the Baba was checking a container with Nagaland number plate when a truck bearing Rajasthan number plate hit the container from behind. Baba died after being caught in the collision. 4. PM Modi becomes longest-serving head of government Prime Minister Narendra Modi has become the longest-serving head of government in India. By completing 8,931 days as head of government, both as Chief Minister of Gujarat and as Prime Minister 5. Shringar Gauri temple opens after a year: 2 km queues as women raise ‘Free Gyanvapi’ slogans, Australian devotee joins chants A large number of devotees gathered on Sunday for darshan at the Maa Shringar Gauri temple inside Varanasi’s Gyanvapi complex, with queues stretching nearly 2 km. The temple opens for devotees only once a year on the fourth day of Chaitra Navratri, and will now reopen next year. 6. Accused held in Varanasi BSc student killing: Police carry accused to court after chase; students clash with ADM The accused in the murder of a student at UP College in Varanasi was produced in court under tight security on Saturday evening. Police feared that lawyers and students might assault the accused. Therefore, the police tried to make him run, but he stumbled because his leg was fractured. Following this, police personnel carried him into the courtroom. 7. LPG from US, crude from Russia reach India A cargo ship carrying liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) from Texas, US, arrived at Mangalore Port on Sunday. Meanwhile, a ship from Russia carrying crude oil also reached India. 8. Fake IAS has married not once but 25 times: Victim's father alleges serial marriage fraud; vows to get justice for his daughter The paralysed father from Gorakhpur alleges the fake IAS accused married 25 times, extorting money, and ruined his daughter’s life. Speaking anonymously to Dainik Bhaskar, he said he is determined to ensure strict punishment and explained how the family fell into the trap, how the marriage was arranged, and how the truth later surfaced. 9. Film ‘Dhurandhar’ sparks row over Atiq Ahmed portrayal: Chargesheet in Umesh Pal Murder mentions Pakistan link A brief 7–8-minute appearance by a character named Atif Ahmed in the film Dhurandhar: The Revenge has sparked a political and factual debate. The reel character closely resembles the real-life mafia don Atiq Ahmed from Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh. The film recreates his murder in a manner strikingly similar to the killing of Atiq and his brother Ashraf in April 2023, while attributing the sequence of events to a conspiracy involving National Security Advisor Ajay Sanyal. 10. Air travel prices may go up soon, Civil Aviation Ministry lifts airfare cap Airline companies will be able to increase domestic flight fares according to seat demand as the Civil Aviation Ministry has removed the cap on airfares.

stories.title: BJP core committee meets at Deputy CM’s residence:First such instance in 9 years; Yogi yet to return from Noida
stories.summary: A BJP core committee meeting has begun at the Lucknow residence of UP Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath was on a visit to Noida today and has not yet returned to Lucknow. The meeting is being held in his absence, and members may later move to the Chief Minister’s residence after his arrival. Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya, BJP state president Pankaj Chaudhary, and organisation general secretary Dharampal Singh are present at the meeting. This is the first time in nine years of the Yogi government that a core committee meeting is being held at a Deputy CM’s residence. Earlier, such meetings were always held at the CM’s official residence at 5 Kalidas Marg or at the BJP state headquarters. No core committee meeting has ever been held at Keshav Prasad Maurya’s residence. However, before the 2022 Assembly elections, CM Yogi Adityanath, RSS leader Dattatreya Hosabale, Krishna Gopal, and others had visited his residence for a meal after a coordination meeting at the CM’s house. Roadmap to be prepared at Brajesh Pathak’s residence In the core committee meeting, a roadmap will be drawn to implement decisions taken in the coordination meeting between the RSS, government, and BJP. The BJP has assured the RSS that district executive bodies in all districts will be formed by March 30. The party’s state team will be constituted by April 15. Political appointments in all corporations, commissions, and boards will be completed by May 15. According to sources, discussions will also focus on forming the OBC Commission for panchayat elections, political appointments and the state team structure.

stories.title: Power struggle stalls BJP district president appointments in UP:Disputes between top leaders over candidates delay naming district chiefs in 5 areas
stories.summary: The politics of Purvanchal is considered incomplete without caste and pressure politics. This time BJP appears to be caught in this political maze. The party's stalwarts have linked their prestige to the appointment of 5 district presidents in Purvanchal. In Chandauli, there is an open tussle between Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and former state president Mahendranath Pandey. In Deoria, the egos of 2 former state presidents (Surya Pratap Shahi and Ramapati Ram Tripathi) clashed. While in Gorakhpur-Varanasi, CM Yogi and PM Modi's likes and dislikes have completely stalled the matter. This is also affecting the party's functioning. What is the reason for this tug of war? With less than a year left for assembly elections, when will the 5 district presidents be announced? Read in our special report... First District - Chandauli District President appointment stuck between Brahmin vs Thakur Chandauli is the home district of former Union Minister Dr. Mahendranath Pandey and Defence Minister Rajnath Singh. Party sources say Pandey wants to remove the current district president, Kashi Singh. He wishes to appoint a Brahmin face as president. Their camp believes that Kashi Singh did not work properly in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. Even after being the Kshatriya district president, the Thakurs voted for SP. This led to the defeat of two-time MP Dr. Mahendranath Pandey. Kashi Singh belongs to the Defence Minister's camp. Now the announcement of the district president is stuck in the tug of war between Rajnath Singh and Dr. Mahendranath's camps. The special thing is that the party had made Pandey the in-charge of state organisational elections. Under his supervision, 93 district presidents have been declared in the organisational elections. However, the appointment of the district president is stuck in his home district itself. Second District - Deoria Ramapati says, ‘Whoever I advocate for will become president’ In Deoria, Pintu Jaiswal, a close associate of former state president Ramapati Ram Tripathi and Sadar block chief, was almost certain to become the district president. Tripathi had also approved Jaiswal's name to state president Pankaj Chaudhary. However, Agriculture Minister Surya Pratap Shahi, MP Shashank Mani Tripathi and 2 local MLAs opposed Pintu's appointment. However, in the case Ramapati Ram Tripathi says, ‘I did not ask anyone to make Pintu Jaiswal the district president’. Ask whoever is saying this and why they are saying so. As far as advocacy is concerned, if I advocated for someone, they would definitely become president. The argument against Pintu was that he joined the BJP in 2021 before the panchayat elections. The party made him block chief. Now, if I were made district president, it would send the wrong message to workers. This matter went from Lucknow to Delhi, and Pintu could not become the district president. Now the party is looking for a name that everyone agrees on. Third District - Ambedkarnagar State President looking for a Kurmi-Brahmin face BJP wanted to promote district vice president Rana Randhir Singh to make him president here. However, state president Pankaj Chaudhary's argument was that Faizabad division is a Kurmi and Brahmin-dominated area. SP has Kurmi and Brahmin leaders here. The party has only appointed a Kurmi district president in Barabanki of Faizabad division. Not a single Brahmin has been made district president. In such a situation, Chaudhary suggested making a Kurmi or Brahmin face the district president instead of Rana, which would help in securing the vote bank. This is the reason why the announcement of the district president's name could not be made in Ambedkar Nagar as well. Fourth District - Varanasi District President will be appointed based on PM's preference Hansraj Vishwakarma is the district president in Prime Minister Narendra Modi's parliamentary constituency, Varanasi. The party has also made him a Member of the Legislative Council (MLC). Active in politics for 34 years, Hansraj is an important face of the backward classes in the area. Therefore, a search is on for a strong alternative to replace him. According to sources, the decision of the district president in Varanasi will only be made after Prime Minister Narendra Modi's green signal. It is by the Prime Minister's wish that Hansraj has remained district president for three terms. Fifth District - Gorakhpur Metropolitan President passed away last June In March 2025, Devesh Srivastava was declared Metropolitan President in Gorakhpur. However, he passed away from a heart attack in June 2025. Now the position of Metropolitan President is vacant here. There is no political manoeuvring happening here. The Metropolitan President will be appointed only with CM Yogi's preference. Therefore, everyone is waiting for his signal. 93 names approved so far BJP has divided UP into 98 organisational districts. The party released the first list of 70 district presidents on March 16, 2025. Devesh Srivastava, the district president of Gorakhpur, included in this list, passed away in June 2025. Meanwhile, Gonda district president Amar Kishore Kashyap was removed after a video of him with a female worker went viral in the party office. This left 68 district presidents. After this, 14 more names came forward on November 26 and 11 district presidents on February 26 this year. In this, Iqbal Bahadur Tiwari was made president in Gonda. However, the appointment of district presidents in Chandauli, Deoria, Varanasi, Ambedkar Nagar and Gorakhpur has not been made yet.

stories.title: Akhilesh says, 'women will get ₹40,000 if party forms govt':SP chief hits out at ‘Dhurandhar’, claiming BJP funding films
stories.summary: “These people have decided on a cabinet expansion during Navratri. It is just an attempt to pacify those who are upset. Now that the budget has been fully spent, they are making ministers. Funds are being released quickly to several departments. One department has even approved tenders worth ₹1,000 crore, but it is unclear what has actually been delivered,” said SP chief Akhilesh Yadav on Sunday, taking a swipe at the Yogi government’s likely cabinet expansion. Akhilesh was speaking at the Murti Devi–Malti Devi Women Honour Ceremony in Lucknow, where several women were felicitated. His wife and Mainpuri MP Dimple Yadav were also present. He reiterated that if voted to power, his party would give ₹40,000 annually to women and revive the Samajwadi pension scheme. Amid the controversy over the film ‘Dhurandhar’, he alleged that the BJP is now funding films to defame opposition parties. The film ‘Dhurandhar: The Revenge’, released on March 19, features a character named Atif Ahmed, resembling real-life mafia Atiq Ahmed. Leaders from Congress and SP have termed the film propaganda. Dimple Yadav said that in the “new India”, women feel unsafe and fearful. Referring to the Ankita Bhandari case in Uttarakhand, she said such incidents leave deep wounds and raise concerns about the country’s progress. Key points from Akhilesh’s speech: 1. ‘Not a green corridor, but a wasted corridor’ in Lucknow Akhilesh said the Defence Minister wants to do good work for Lucknow, but CM Yogi has built a “wasted corridor” instead of a green corridor. He claimed it lacks space for pedestrians and does not meet proper standards, despite costing ₹7,000 crore. 2. ‘Election setting has already begun in UP’ He alleged that preparations and “settings” for elections have already started in UP, including the posting of officials. He also claimed irregularities in previous elections. 3. ‘LPG cylinder depends on luck now’ Mocking the situation, he said getting an LPG cylinder depends on luck, otherwise people must stand in queues. He also accused BJP leaders of irregularities in cylinder distribution. 4. ‘Law and order have collapsed in UP’ Akhilesh blamed the administration and police for deteriorating law and order, citing incidents in Gorakhpur, Varanasi and Mathura. He alleged political misuse of the police and rising corruption. 5. ‘PDA strength troubling BJP’ He claimed that the strength of PDA (backward, Dalit, minority alliance) is worrying the BJP, and alleged plans of large-scale deployments and election manipulation. 6. ‘If Shankaracharya not spared, anyone can be insulted’ He criticised police actions, saying if even religious leaders like Shankaracharya are not spared, anyone can be insulted. He also questioned the process of appointing the DGP.

stories.title: Shringar Gauri temple opens after a year:2 km queues as women raise ‘Free Gyanvapi’ slogans, Australian devotee joins chants
stories.summary: A large number of devotees gathered on Sunday for darshan at the Maa Shringar Gauri temple inside Varanasi’s Gyanvapi complex, with queues stretching nearly 2 km. The temple opens for devotees only once a year on the fourth day of Chaitra Navratri, and will now reopen next year. The four women plaintiffs in the Gyanvapi case also arrived to offer prayers, raising slogans of “Free Gyanvapi”. They have moved court seeking recognition of the site as a temple. Tight security arrangements were in place due to the heavy footfall, with devotees allowed entry under strict supervision. During the 25-minute worship, vermillion and sandalwood paste were applied to the ancient, damaged stones of the shrine, while mantras were chanted. The premises echoed with chants of “Har Har Mahadev”, accompanied by damru beats. Among the devotees was Maria from Australia, who joined in chanting praises of the Goddess. See 3 photos... Regular worship banned after 1992 Regular darshan and worship of Maa Shringar Gauri continued until 1992. Following the Babri demolition in Ayodhya, access was restricted due to security concerns. Since then, the temple has been opened for darshan only once a year, on the fourth day of Chaitra Navratri. On August 18, 2021, five women filed a petition in a Varanasi court seeking permission for regular worship at the site. Acting on court orders, a survey was later conducted within the premises. After the survey, the Hindu side claimed that a Shivling was found in the basement, while the Muslim side maintained that it was a fountain. The petition is led by Delhi-based Rakhi Singh. The other petitioners—Sita Sahu, Manju Vyas, Laxmi Devi and Rekha Pathak—are residents of Varanasi.
