stories.title: Woman kills mother-in-law in Lucknow:Planned murder as robbery, strangled victim at home
stories.summary: Shocking details have emerged in the murder of a 69-year-old woman in Lucknow. Police revealed that the accused daughter-in-law, Ranjana Verma (36), and her 21-year-old lover Rajan Sharma had planned the killing three days in advance. During interrogation, both admitted they intended to make the crime appear like a robbery. After strangling the victim, they removed her jewellery and hid it. Police have since recovered the items based on their statements. The incident took place in Nishatganj under the Mahanagar Police Station area. Body discovered at home, last rites performed On 21 March, the body of Nirmala Devi (69) was found inside her home. Police, assisted by a sniffer dog, cracked the case within a day and arrested both accused on Sunday. Family members have since performed her last rites at Bhaisakund Cremation Ground. The accused woman’s 18-year-old son and two daughters remain at home with their father. Family background and living arrangement Nirmala Devi lived in Nishatganj, Lane No. 3, with her son Trish Verma (40), daughter-in-law Ranjana, grandson Aditya, and granddaughters Anshika (15) and Sanvi (1.5 years). Her husband, Rajaram Verma, a retired Secretariat employee, had died two years ago. Trish works on contract at Qila Power House in the electricity department, while the grandson is employed as a delivery boy. The family occupies the ground floor of a two-storey house, with eight tenants residing on the first floor. Rajan Sharma, the accused lover, was one of these tenants. Grandson discovers the body On the day of the incident, Trish was on duty, while Ranjana and her younger daughter were at home. The grandson returned around 4 pm and found his grandmother lying unconscious with her hands and feet tied. He raised an alarm, drawing neighbours to the scene. They confirmed that Nirmala Devi had died. The grandson informed his father and called his mother, who returned home shortly afterwards along with Rajan. Sniffer dog and CCTV raise suspicion During the investigation, a forensic team and dog squad were deployed. The sniffer dog stopped near Rajan, raising immediate suspicion. Further scrutiny revealed that CCTV cameras in the house had been switched off between 2 pm and 4 pm. This strengthened police suspicion of internal involvement. Footage after 4 pm showed Ranjana outside with Rajan, prompting police to detain both for questioning. Affair led to tensions within family Police investigations revealed that Rajan, originally from Gauraya Kuri Shivan in Bihar, had been living as a tenant in the house for three years. Within a few months, he developed a close relationship with Ranjana, which later turned into an affair. The family, including Nirmala Devi and her son, had become aware of the relationship. Frequent arguments followed, with Nirmala often supporting her son. She had reportedly started cooking separately just three days before the incident. Execution of the crime According to police, on the day of the murder, Ranjana called Rajan home. Together, they tied Nirmala Devi’s hands and feet and strangled her. To avoid suspicion, they switched off the CCTV cameras before committing the crime and later fled in a car. After some distance, they remotely switched the cameras back on using a mobile phone. However, when the family began calling, they panicked and returned home. Background of the accused lover Assistant Commissioner of Police stated that Rajan claimed to have been a member of an Under-16 cricket team, though he quit after not being selected further. He had been financially supported by Ranjana, who helped him purchase a car that he used as a taxi. Police are now verifying his claims regarding his cricket background as part of the ongoing investigation.

stories.title: Yogi Cabinet to meet today, 23 proposals to be discussed:Council of Ministers meeting also scheduled; poll agenda to be shared
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will chair a cabinet meeting today. More than 23 proposals will be discussed in the meeting. A proposal for the formation of an OBC commission for the Panchayat elections may also be discussed. However, it has not been included in the agenda released for the cabinet. Chief Secretary SP Goyal released the agenda for the cabinet meeting to be held at 11 am in Lok Bhawan. it includes 10 proposals from the Infrastructure and Industrial Development department. It also includes a proposal for a private business park. The government has launched the 'UP Private Business Park Development Scheme-2025', which aims to assist the private sector in developing industrial parks. The government will provide loans at 1% interest and create a revolving fund of Rs 2500 crore. Such a park is being prepared for development in Bhauti, Kanpur, which will increase investment, help in easy establishment of industries and generate new employment opportunities. After the cabinet meeting, there will be a meeting of the council of ministers, which will discuss government's 9 years of achievements and coordination with workers. stories.title: Only 40% bloom on mango trees in Malihabad:Cold weather delays crop, farmers say, 'prices likely to rise this season'
stories.summary: Malihabad, widely known as the ‘mango belt’ of Uttar Pradesh, mango trees have begun to flower. However, farmers are worried as blossoms are visible on only 40–50% of the trees this season. To encourage flowering, farmers have been spraying medicines across orchards. This marks a sharp decline from last year, when nearly 80% of trees were covered with blossoms by mid-March, resulting in a strong yield. Experts say weather variability is a key factor behind the reduced flowering this year. Natural cycles and weather influence production Renowned horticulturist Haji Kaleem Ullah Khan, popularly known as the ‘Mango Man of India’ and a Padma Shri awardee, explains that flowering depends on rainfall, temperature and humidity. According to him, it is natural for mango trees to show reduced blossoming once every one to two years. His orchard, ‘Abdullah Nursery’, features over 700 varieties of mango across more than 100 orchards in the region. Despite a favourable winter, he notes that fluctuating temperatures have delayed fruit development this year. Delayed growth and smaller fruit expected Typically, by the time of Holi, mangoes begin to grow beyond the initial stage. However, this season only blossoms and tiny green grains are visible, which are yet to develop into fruitlets. Kaleem Ullah Khan indicates that while the crop will mature in due course, the fruit size is likely to be smaller than usual. Consumers may not see the large, one-kilogram Dasheri mango this year. The final yield remains uncertain, as the conversion of blossoms into fruitlets is progressing slowly. Impact of orchard conditions and airflow According to Khan, mango orchards require adequate exposure to warm air to ensure proper taste and juiciness. In densely grown orchards, trees often fail to receive natural airflow. Dew accumulates on leaves instead of reaching the ground, which can affect both flavour and texture. He suggests that orchards planted at higher levels (10–15 feet elevation) tend to perform better due to improved environmental exposure. Use of chemicals and reduced yield estimates Khan’s son, Azeem Khan, highlights the role of chemical sprays in sustaining flowering levels. He states that while last year saw 80–85% flowering, this year it is around 60%, largely due to the use of a stimulant known locally as ‘Kanta’. He notes that while such chemicals can induce flowering, they may also harm the trees in the long run. Typically, orchard owners avoid such methods, but contractors managing orchards for short periods often resort to them. Overall, he estimates that Malihabad may see only 40–50% of its usual yield this season, which could drive up prices. Weather risks: Storms and rain remain key threats Farmers are currently relieved that there has been no significant rainfall, as excessive rain can damage blossoms by turning them black and increasing humidity. However, the coming weeks remain critical. Azeem Khan warns that storms or rainfall in the next month could severely impact the crop, making protection of blossoms the primary challenge for growers. Similar trends in nearby regions The situation is not limited to Malihabad. Mango growers in nearby areas such as Kakori and Mal are also reporting reduced flowering and similar concerns about weather-related risks. Farmers from these regions supply produce to the Lucknow market, particularly Dubagga Mandi, while some export mangoes through corporate contracts. Market outlook: Likely price rise Mangoes from Malihabad are expected to arrive in markets after 20 May. Traders anticipate a price increase due to lower production. Trader Suraj Prasad Yadav explains that last year, initial wholesale prices for Dasheri mangoes were around ₹40 per kg, dropping to ₹20 within weeks. This year, prices could be at least ₹10 higher due to reduced supply. Official assessment of the situation Krishna Mohan Chaudhary, Deputy Director of the Horticulture Department in Uttar Pradesh, states that current weather conditions are still favourable. However, he cautions that rainfall could damage the crop by causing fungal issues such as ‘Dahiya disease’. He adds that fluctuations in temperature often result in varying levels of flowering each year, making such variations a recurring pattern in mango cultivation. Now know about Malihabad's mangoes

stories.title: Weather set to change across UP:Rain in 10 districts, alert for 20 more; statewide showers likely from March 26
stories.summary: It has been raining in Uttar Pradesh for the past week. Since Monday morning, 10 districts have received light rain, including Noida, Ghaziabad, Meerut and Bareilly, while Sambhal received heavy rain along with strong winds. Rain alert for 20 districts today The Meteorological Department has issued a rain alert for 20 districts today, mostly in West UP. At the same time, the weather remains clear in Purvanchal districts, with light sunshine and a cool breeze in the air. Weather to remain unstable in Western UP According to the department, Western UP will see unstable weather throughout the day, with intermittent rains. From Tuesday, a change in weather is expected and temperatures may rise by 4 to 7 degrees Celsius. Another system to bring fresh spell of rain A new Western Disturbance will become active from March 26. This may bring rain again across the entire state for 3 to 4 days. Temperature variation seen across districts In the last 24 hours, light rain was recorded in 10 districts including Barabanki and Maharajganj. Lakhimpur Kheri recorded the highest temperature at 33 degrees Celsius, while Kanpur was the coldest with a minimum temperature of 13.7 degrees Celsius. Lucknow's meteorologist Atul Singh said- Due to the effect of a very weak western disturbance, western UP is cloudy today. Intermittent rain is occurring. The weather will remain clear for the next 2-3 days. Temperatures will gradually rise. However, a new spell of rain will begin across the entire state from March 26. See pictures- How will the weather be for the next 3 days? Know the weather conditions in West UP- Damage to wheat, arhar crops due to storm, how to protect Agricultural experts say that rain and strong winds have affected Rabi, Zaid, and horticultural crops. At this time, pods are forming and grains are filling in arhar (pigeon pea), mustard, gram, peas, moong (green gram), and groundnut. Strong winds can cause pods to burst and grains to shed. The wheat crop can also fall due to strong winds, posing a risk of reduced yield. Among vegetables, the flowers and small fruits of okra, tomato, bottle gourd, cucumber, watermelon, muskmelon, eggplant, and chili can fall. Farmers have been advised to immediately harvest the ripened crop and store it in a safe place. Do not allow water to accumulate in the fields; for this, arrange for proper drainage.

stories.title: KC Tyagi joins RLD after nearly two decades:Jayant Chaudhary inducts him in party, calls return natural, aims to revive party base in western UP
stories.summary: Veteran leader KC Tyagi, who spent nearly two decades with Janata Dal (United), joined the Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD) on Sunday. The induction took place in Delhi, where RLD National President Jayant Chaudhary formally welcomed Tyagi and his son Amrish Tyagi into the party. Tyagi remarked that his political journey had originally begun with the Lok Dal, and therefore, his return to RLD felt natural. He said there was ‘no difference’ between JDU and RLD, noting that leaders like Nitish Kumar and Chaudhary Charan Singh had once been aligned in their political vision. ‘RLD was always in my heart’ In a conversation, Tyagi said that even during his tenure outside the RLD, he continued to raise issues associated with Chaudhary Charan Singh and the party’s ideology. He emphasised that both JDU and RLD share similar manifestos and roots in the Lok Dal tradition. He recalled his long association with leaders such as George Fernandes, Sharad Yadav, and Nitish Kumar, all of whom were once part of Chaudhary Charan Singh’s Lok Dal. No ambition for posts, focus on legacy Tyagi clarified that his decision to join RLD was not driven by any desire for a position. He stated that he has already worked with several prominent leaders, including Chaudhary Charan Singh, George Fernandes, Devi Lal, V. P. Singh, Chandra Shekhar, and Karpoori Thakur. According to him, his primary aim now is to strengthen the unresolved issues linked to Chaudhary Charan Singh’s legacy and support those carrying it forward. Strategy for 2027 elections Outlining his plans, Tyagi said the goal is to make RLD strong once again, particularly in western Uttar Pradesh. He expressed his intention to empower Jayant Chaudhary and restore the party’s influence to the level it enjoyed during Chaudhary Charan Singh’s era. Having contested six elections from western UP, and winning multiple times, Tyagi said he would focus on rebuilding the party’s base in the region. ‘No one like him’ Reflecting on his long association with Nitish Kumar, Tyagi described him as a friend of 52 years and extended his best wishes to him and his family. He added, however, that “there is no one like Nitish Kumar”. Ashok Yadav also joins RLD Former Uttar Pradesh minister Ashok Yadav also joined the RLD on Sunday along with his supporters. He served as MLA from the Shikohabad constituency in Firozabad between 2007 and 2012, winning as an independent candidate. Apart from his political career, Yadav was in the news in 2019 due to serious criminal allegations, including charges of rape and extortion, which led to police action.

stories.title: Jobs of 1.86 lakh UP teachers at risk:Take UP-TET exam or complete SIR and census targets
stories.summary: In UP, 1.86 lakh teachers have not passed the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET). These teachers are from primary (Class 1 to 5) and upper primary (Class 6 to 8) schools. Among them, 50 thousand are such who cannot even appear for the exam due to not having the minimum qualification. The Supreme Court has set a deadline of September 2027 for passing TET. In such a situation, UPTET-2026, which will be held in July after four years in UP, is a big opportunity for teachers. The difficulty is that these teachers, entangled in the puzzle of SIR (Special Intensive Revision), do not understand when they will prepare for the exam amidst their duties for the national census in May? What is the exam schedule, why is it necessary for teachers to pass TET? What conditions has the Service Selection Commission added for teachers in UPTET? Why are teacher unions opposing the TET, which has been made mandatory for teachers employed before 2011? Read this report UPTET is happening after 4 years The Uttar Pradesh Education Service Selection Commission announced the schedule for the primary and upper primary level examinations on March 20. This examination is going to be held in UP after 4 years. Earlier, the application process for the examination started in 2021, but the examination could only be held in 2022. This time, 15 to 20 lakh applicants can participate in the examination. This includes 1.86 lakh teachers who are working in council schools without passing TET. One time registration mandatory The Education Service Selection Commission has made One Time Registration (OTR) mandatory for UPTET applications. All new applicants will first have to complete One Time Registration. Only after this will they be able to apply to participate in the examination. Applicants who have previously completed One Time Registration will only need to apply using their login-password. How 1.86 lakh teachers got stuck in the TET tangle Parliament passed the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act (RTE-2009) on August 4, 2009. It was implemented nationwide from April 1, 2010. Its objective is to provide free and compulsory education to every child aged 6 to 14 years, from class 1 to 8. Additionally, TET was made mandatory as a minimum qualification for teachers. By issuing an order on July 27, 2011, TET was made a mandatory service condition for recruitment at primary and secondary levels. However, on September 1, 2025, a bench of Supreme Court Justices Dipankar Datta and Manmohan ruled that all teachers with more than 5 years of service remaining would be required to pass TET within 2 years (by September 2027). Those with less service were exempted, but they too were made to pass TET for promotion. Along with this, the double bench also questioned the 2014 Karnataka Pramati Educational and Cultural Trust judgment, which granted complete exemption to minority institutions (aided or unaided) from the RTE Act. The court stated that a review of the Pramati Trust judgment is necessary. The matter was referred to a constitutional bench. Currently, the constitutional bench has not been constituted. Teacher organizations argue that the mandatory nature of TET under RTE-2009 came into effect from July 2011. In such a situation, how can it be applied to teachers appointed before this? Many teachers have been teaching for 20 to 25 years. They say that taking an exam again after so many years of service is not reasonable. Following the Supreme Court's order, 2.1 million such teachers across the country were forced to agitate. Under the pressure of the deaths of two teachers in UP and the teachers' agitation, the Uttar Pradesh government filed a review petition before the Supreme Court's double bench, comprising Justice Dipankar Datta and Justice Augustine George Masih, which is yet to be heard. New Condition Added for Teachers Applying As per the Supreme Court's directive, it is mandatory for the 1.86 lakh teachers of the state to also pass TET. If they do not pass TET before September 2027, they will have to be dismissed from service. Consequently, the Uttar Pradesh Education Service Selection Commission has added some conditions to the application for teachers as well. In the UPTET application, it will have to be stated whether you are a working government teacher. If 'Yes' is selected, you will have to fill in the type of teacher, name of the organization/school, joining date, retirement date, and Human Sampada Code. Additionally, the latest salary slip will also have to be uploaded at the time of application. 83 Marks will be the passing marks for EWS, similar to reserved categories The Uttar Pradesh Education Service Selection Commission has made a significant change in the EWS category this time. EWS has also been placed in the reserved category. This means applicants from the EWS category will need to score a minimum of 83 marks to pass UPTET. Last time, in the 2022 examination, EWS candidates were required to score 90 marks for passing. 50 thousand teachers cannot even appear for TET The mandatory educational qualification for UPTET has created a major crisis for approximately 50 thousand teachers. They do not even have the eligibility to appear for UPTET. According to Dr. Prabhakant Mishra, District President of the Junior High School Teachers' Association, Lucknow, until 1998, the minimum qualification for teacher recruitment in primary and secondary schools in the state was Intermediate and a two-year BTC. Approximately 15-20 thousand teachers are working in the state with this minimum qualification. Additionally, there are more than 15 thousand teachers who are dependents of deceased employees. After 5 years of service, they receive a trained grade as per government order. Many among them are neither graduates nor BTC pass. The third category includes people working as teachers with B.P.Ed. In the state, B.P.Ed holders were appointed as physical education teachers in primary and secondary schools in 1999 and 2004. The number of such teachers is also around 20 thousand.

stories.title: Long queues at petrol pumps, scuffles in Gonda:People arrive with large containers; govt warns of action against rumour spreaders
stories.summary: In Uttar Pradesh, queues have formed at petrol pumps. On Friday, the third day of rumours about fuel running out, people continued to arrive carrying large cans and drums to fill petrol and diesel, waiting for hours due to the crowd. At Kathauta Chowk in Lucknow, the line for petrol and diesel stretches 500 metres. In Dhanepur, Gonda, a scuffle broke out at a petrol pump as people jostled to get diesel, with some pulling each other out of the queue. The Yogi government clarified on Thursday that fuel supply is completely normal and there is no need to worry about petrol or diesel. The situation is fully under control. Ranveer Prasad, Principal Secretary of Food and Logistics, said there is no crisis anywhere and fuel is being provided as per demand in all districts. Strict action will be taken against those spreading rumours. There are around 13,168 petrol pumps in the state. Pump owners said the crowd has suddenly increased three to four times. They are unsure why people are panicking despite sufficient fuel availability.

stories.title: Surya Tilak of Ram Lalla lasts 9 minutes on forehead:Panchamrit Abhishek completed, idol in gold-embroidered yellow attire; 10 lakh devotees gather in Ayodhya
stories.summary: In Ayodhya, on Ram Navami, Ram Lalla received the Surya Tilak at 12 noon on Friday. This is the second Surya Tilak after his Prana Pratishtha. The ceremony was held at the Abhijit Muhurat. Blue rays fell on the Lord’s forehead for nine minutes. Prime Minister Modi watched the Surya Tilak on TV. With the Surya Tilak, Ram Lalla’s divine birth was celebrated. Fourteen priests performed special rituals inside the sanctum, followed by an aarti. After the Tilak, the curtain over Ram Lalla was closed briefly. Ram Lalla will now receive offerings of 56 types of food. For the Surya Tilak, a 65-foot-long system of 20 pipes made of Ashtadhatu was set up. Four lenses and four mirrors directed the rays onto Ram Lalla’s forehead. Earlier, the sanctum was decorated with flowers. At 5:30 am, an aarti was performed, and the Lord was dressed in a yellow robe. Devotees will now have three extra hours to view Ram Lalla, from 5 am to 11 pm, instead of the usual 6:30 am to 9:30 pm. See these 3 pictures related to Surya Tilak 2024 Special food offerings for the Ram Lalla Following the symbolic birth of Lord Ram, a grand offering of 56 varieties of food will be presented to the deity. This includes fruit-based fasting dishes and preparations made from buckwheat flour and water chestnut flour, along with coriander and amaranth-based sweet mixtures. The total offering will weigh around 10 quintals, which will later be distributed among devotees as blessed food. Security measures and Live broadcast VIP entry will be restricted for half an hour before and after the Surya Tilak ceremony. At the time of the ritual, 14 specially designated priests will be present inside the sanctum. The event will be broadcast live, with six cameras installed inside the temple premises. All routes leading to the temple have been covered with red carpets. Technology behind the Surya Tilak This is the second time the Surya Tilak ceremony is being performed, the first being in 2024. The system enabling this event was developed by scientists from Bengaluru. According to temple trustee Dr. Anil Mishra, specially installed equipment reflects sunlight in a way that forms a mark on the deity’s forehead, lasting for about four minutes. The nine-day festival, also known as Chaitra Navratri, concludes on Ram Navami, which marks the birthday of Lord Ram. Throughout the festival, all nine days are devoted to honouring the nine incarnations of the goddess Shakti. The festival is celebrated with great devotion across India, with rituals and prayers honouring the goddess in her various forms. Ram Navami is the day when Lord Rama appeared in his human and divine form, and is celebrated with great reverence and festivities all over India, but especially in the sacred city of Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh. Leading up to Ram Navami, Hindus observe the 9-day fast during the Chaitra Navaratri, which consists of abstinence from alcohol, smoking, consumption of sattvic vegetarian food and immersing oneself in prayer and meditation.

stories.title: Rain in six districts, alert in 38:Clouds over 10 cities, cool winds blowing, bad weather to continue for 5 days
stories.summary: Weather conditions across Uttar Pradesh shifted on Friday morning, with rainfall reported in six districts—Lucknow, Kanpur, Ayodhya, Sitapur, Bareilly, and Sambhal. Around 10 cities, including Noida, Agra, and Meerut, experienced cloudy skies. Winds reaching speeds of up to 30 km/h have added a chill to the air, leading to a noticeable dip in temperatures. Alert issued in 38 districts; western disturbance behind shift The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a rain alert for 38 districts across the state. According to officials, the change in weather is due to the impact of a western disturbance. The department has warned that unstable weather conditions will persist for the next five days. There is also a possibility of hailstorms and strong winds in isolated areas. Temperature fluctuations recorded across the state Over the past 24 hours, the state’s average temperature has increased by up to 5°C. Banda recorded the highest maximum temperature at 40.2°C, while Muzaffarnagar registered the lowest temperature at 15.4°C. Expert insight: More rain and Strong winds ahead Lucknow-based meteorologist Atul Singh stated that winds originating from Pakistan have entered Uttar Pradesh, triggering light rainfall. He added that another western disturbance will become active on March 29, likely bringing widespread rainfall across the state. Wind speeds could increase to 40–50 km/h, and temperatures may drop by up to 3°C. See 3 weather pictures 5-day weather forecast for Uttar Pradesh

stories.title: Chandauli SDM’s mother alleges daughter-in-law threw acid:Says she took jewellery worth ₹40 lakh; wanted them sent to old-age home
stories.summary: The domestic dispute between SDM couple Anupam Mishra and Divya Ojha in Chandauli is getting complicated. Divya's father has accused Anupam of being impotent in the FIR. **Dainik Bhaskar** spoke to Shashi Mishra, mother of SDM Anupam Mishra. During this, Shashi Mishra made several shocking claims. She said - son Anupam had a love marriage. There is no question of dowry. On the contrary, we gave jewelry worth lakhs and a car to our daughter-in-law. Divya used to assault us. She had thrown acid on me. As for being impotent, after living together for 6 years, she found out that her husband is impotent? Shashi Mishra gave a point-by-point reply to the allegations of Nishikant Ojha, father of SDM Divya Allegation 1 - Demand for dowry As soon as the marriage was fixed, Anupam and his family demanded dowry. Initially, the demand was for 20 crore rupees. When refused, it gradually came down to a demand for 1 crore rupees cash, a wedding in a 5-star hotel, and a Fortuner car. We deposited 10 lakh rupees into the account before the engagement. After the wedding, we had to give 28 lakh cash, jewelry worth 40 lakh, and goods worth 7 lakh. Shashi Mishra's reply - My son had a love marriage, so there was never any talk of dowry. On the contrary, we gave jewelry to our daughter-in-law at the wedding. Today their value would be around 40 lakh. The daughter-in-law took all the jewelry with her. We also got a Creta car. My husband paid 2.56 lakh rupees, which is half the payment. There is also an entry in the passbook. She took all of that, we have nothing left now. Regarding the 28 lakh cash, how did they give it? Allegation 2 - Attempted Murder Upon not receiving the desired dowry, daughter Divya was subjected to physical and mental torture. On the night of December 7, 2025, at 2 AM, Anupam, along with his mother, launched a deadly attack on Divya. Shashi Mishra's response- Neither I nor my son ever laid a hand on my daughter-in-law. She was the one who used to hit me, Anupam, and Anupam's father. I used to serve her, massage her hands and feet. She wanted my son not to stay with me. She used to say, "Send your parents to an old age home." In winters, she would lock the house. We all used to stay outside in the cold. On the night of December 7, my daughter-in-law threw an acid bottle at me. Fortunately, the acid fell on the ground, but pieces of the bottle got embedded in my face and hand. I was treated at PHC Chandauli. I had a 2-inch wound, and I have the report too. The next day, my daughter-in-law and her father, along with 4-5 people, vandalized the house. They hit me and my son. Divya's father pushed me down and tried to strangle me. After this, they took away jewelry worth 40 lakh and my son's passport. We had complained at Alinagar police station in Chandauli, but an FIR was not registered. After this, my son filed for divorce in the Allahabad Family Court. Allegation 3- Anupam is congenitally impotent Anupam is congenitally impotent. This fact was hidden from us during the marriage. When our daughter talked about having children and treatment, she was beaten. Divya was threatened to quit her job and stay at home. Shashi Mishra's response- For 6 years of marriage, Divya didn't realize he was impotent? Both used to visit Leh-Ladakh, Nainital, Mussoorie, etc. They spent time together, both were very happy. It didn't seem at all that she was unhappy with my son. Now, after 6 years, Divya's father is making such a vile accusation against my son. Accusation 4 - Jewels, clothes seized The daughter's entire 'Stridhan' (woman's property), jewelry, clothes, and other belongings were kept by Divya's in-laws. They were not returned despite repeated requests. Shashi Mishra's response- Firstly, we didn't receive anything from their side, so what would we keep in our possession? On the contrary, she has taken away the jewelry we gave her after beating us. She has locked everything in her government house. We have nothing. The items in the house like the sofa, bed, wardrobe, all these are government property. We called SDM Divya Ojha's mobile several times to know her side of the story. However, the phone was not answered. We will update as soon as we speak to her. Now know how Anupam and Divya's love story began Anupam Mishra is from Prayagraj and Divya Ojha is from Pratapgarh. Both first met in 2020 at the PCS Training Academy (UP Academy of Administration and Management) in Lucknow. There, they fell in love and got married in December 2020. Everything was fine until 2024, then mutual disagreements began. In December 2025, troubled by quarrels, Anupam Mishra filed for divorce in the Allahabad Family Court. Proceedings on this are ongoing. On March 17, 2026, Divya's father Nishakant Ojha filed an FIR against Anupam at Alinagar police station in Pratapgarh, bringing the matter to light. Both officials have remained silent on the matter.

stories.title: UPSSSC invites applications for 929 posts:Assistant Statistics and Research Officer roles in various departments; apply from April 21
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Subordinate Services Selection Commission (UPSSSC) has released a notification for recruitment to 929 posts of Assistant Statistical Officer and Assistant Research Officer (Statistics) in different state departments. The online application process will begin on April 21 and continue till May 11, while the last date to make corrections and adjust fees is May 18. According to Commission Secretary Avnish Saxena, the recruitment will be carried out across several departments, including State Tax, Forest, Cooperation, Animal Husbandry, Medical and Health, and Irrigation and Water Resources. Out of the total 929 posts, 344 are unreserved, 211 are for Scheduled Castes, 12 for Scheduled Tribes, 300 for OBC, and 62 for Economically Weaker Sections. At the same time, the Commission has also declared the final result of a recruitment exam that had been pending for nearly 10 to 11 years. See this list Result came after 10 years, selection completed for 7 posts UPSSSC has released the final result for the recruitment of 7 posts of Nurse Compounder and Hostel Warden in the Department for Persons with Disabilities. This recruitment was announced in the year 2016, but due to several reasons, the examination and selection process remained pending. The commission declared the final result on Friday. In this, 5 candidates from the unreserved category, 1 from the Scheduled Caste, and 1 from the OBC category have been selected. Regarding the cut-off, it was 48.75 marks for the General category, 39.50 for SC, and 48.25 for OBC. This recruitment process could be completed after nearly 10 years. Result Released After 11 Years, Half the Posts Vacant UPSSSC also released the final result on Friday for the recruitment of 8 posts of Instructor and Stenographer in the Training and Employment Department. The for these posts was issued in the year 2015, but due to several reasons, including the exam and interview not being held on time, the selection process remained pending. In this result, released after nearly 11 years, the commission could not find eligible candidates for all the posts. Only 4 out of 8 posts could be filled. Among the selected candidates, 2 are from the unreserved category, 1 from the Scheduled Caste, and 1 from the OBC category. The remaining posts have remained vacant. Athletics coach to be available after 10 years Youth preparing for athletics in UP will now get a coach after 10 years. UPSSSC has released the recruitment result for one post of Assistant Coach (Athletics) in the Sports Directorate. An for this post was released in 2016, but due to delays in the recruitment process, it took about 10 years for the results to come out. Now, after the completion of the selection process, the department will be able to get an athletics coach.

stories.title: ‘Pawan Singh touched my waist inappropriately’:Career ruined by defamation, Haryanvi actress files complaint with Women’s Commission
stories.summary: Bhojpuri singer and actor Pawan Singh is once again in trouble. Haryanvi actress Anjali Raghav has sent a complaint to the Women's Commission against Pawan Singh for touching her waist. Anjali gathered the courage to complain after the Haryana Women's Commission's strict stance in the case of rapper-singer Badshah. Anjali has also sent evidence related to the matter to the commission via email. Anjali said, That day in Lucknow, Pawan Singh inappropriately touched my waist on stage. This was inappropriate behavior. Not only that, but later, social media and media platforms were systematically used to defame me. Anjali has demanded the commission to remove the objectionable comments made against her on social media. The actress says that because of this, she lost the role of Sita in Delhi Ramlila. On the evening of August 29, 2025, Anjali Raghav and Pawan Singh had a stage performance at a music show in Lucknow. During this performance, Pawan Singh touched Anjali's waist, which was captured on camera. 7 important points of the complaint sent to the commission 1. Remove derogatory posts: Instructions should be given to immediately remove the derogatory posts and false propaganda against me on social media. 2. The role of Sita was taken away: From the age of 16, I used to play the role of Mother Sita in various Ramlilas. Through this, I made my identity. After this controversy, my role in Delhi's Ramlila was taken away. 3. Controversy at Lucknow event: A few months ago, I went to Lucknow for the promotion of one of my songs. There, Bhojpuri singer Pawan Singh touched me on stage without my permission, and his team also made a video of it viral on social media. 4. Raised voice on Instagram, received apology: Breaking my silence, I made information about this incident public through my Instagram account. After this, Pawan Singh publicly apologized to me on social media. At that time, it seemed the matter had settled. 5. PR team continuously threatened: Pawan Singh's PR team continuously threatened me. It was said that my social reputation would be harmed and I would be defamed. Many fake and objectionable posts were made against me. False stories and rumors about me were also spread through some regional media platforms. 6. Claim of Mental Stress and Social Exclusion: Due to these incidents, I had to face mental distress and social humiliation. This also affected my work. I had been playing the role of Mata Sita in Delhi Ramlila for a long time. That role was taken away from me, which was connected to my late mother's last wish. Some people boycotted me and my family, leading to a state of depression. 7. Cyber Police Did Not Take Action: I filed a complaint with the Cyber Police Delhi against the concerned Instagram accounts and media platforms, but the objectionable content has not been removed yet. The commission should immediately remove the objectionable posts and false interviews. Also, a public apology should be arranged from the concerned individuals. Now read... The complete story from touching the waist to trolling Evening of August 29, 2025: Anjali Raghav and Pawan Singh had a stage performance at a music show in Lucknow. During this performance, Pawan Singh touched Anjali's waist, which was captured on camera. Morning of August 30: The video went viral on social media. Anjali reacted for the first time and, through an Instagram story, stated that she was very disturbed mentally. She said that this act was unexpected. Initially, she understood it as a "tag," so she didn't say anything on stage. She announced her decision to leave the Bhojpuri industry. August 30 evening: Anjali's trolling started on social media. Clips of old songs were cut and posted. In these, she was even called a porn star. August 31 morning: Pawan Singh publicly apologised through an Instagram story. He wrote- "My intention was not wrong. If Anjali ji felt bad, I apologize. We are artists and respect each other." August 31 afternoon: Anjali shared that apology and wrote- "Yes, he admitted his mistake and I forgave him." After this, Anjali was pressured by Pawan Singh's PR team to edit the story. She was told to write only "Thank You" instead of "admitted mistake". September 1 2: Within two days, memes, videos, and stories were shared every one to two hours from more than 20 Instagram IDs. In these, obscene comments were made against Anjali. September 3: Anjali approached the Delhi Police. She narrated the events happening with her. She also shared more than 20 Insta IDs with the cyber cell. Who is Anjali Raghav Anjali has made her mark with Haryanvi songs. She has also worked in the Bollywood film Tevar. She has also appeared in the serial 'Carry-Rishta Khatta Meetha'. The song 'Hay Re Meri Moto' brought her worldwide recognition. Anjali has also done many regional music videos. Anjali's live shows are held in Haryana, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, and Delhi. Anjali Raghav has also worked with Pawan Gill in the song 'Madam Nache Nache Re Tu To'.

stories.title: UP TET exam on July 2, 3 and 4:Notification released; forms to be filled from March 27
stories.summary: There is big news for candidates preparing for the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) in UP. The Uttar Pradesh Education Service Selection Commission (UPSSSC) on Friday released the notification for UP-TET 2026 for primary level (Class 1 to 5) and upper primary level (Class 6 to 8). The examination will be held on July 2, 3, and 4. Online applications will be filled from March 27. The last date for submitting forms and fees is April 26. The last date for form correction and fee resolution has been set as May 1. The Commission has stated that this time, a One Time Registration (OTR) system has been implemented in TET. The Commission has advised candidates that it will be mandatory to complete One Time Registration before filling the form. Only after that will they be able to apply for UPTET. The detailed and guidelines are available on the Commission's website, and the application process should be completed only after reading them carefully. Commission said - Do not wait for the last date The commission has made another special appeal to the candidates to complete the application process in time. Do not wait for the last date, so that any technical problem can be avoided. Also, before applying, make sure to get complete information about eligibility and other necessary conditions. 60% passing marks for General and 55% for the Reserved Category Regarding the UP TET exam, the commission has clarified that the marks of the candidates will be released on the official website. The commission has also set the passing criteria. Know what the complete rule is- For General Category: It will be mandatory to score 90 marks out of 150 (60%). Those who score more than this will be given an eligibility certificate. For Reserved Categories (SC/ST/OBC/Disabled etc.): A minimum qualification of 82 marks out of 150 (55%) has been set. Exam will be 150 minutes long, multiple shifts if needed The commission stated that the UP TET exam will be completely objective and, if necessary, can be conducted in more than one shift/day. Exam Pattern Special Arrangement for Normalization If the number of applications is high, the examination may be conducted in more than one shift or day. In such a situation, a normalization process will be applied to equalize the scores of the candidates. The normalization process will be according to the standards set by the commission, and the commission's decision will be final. Now understand the exam pattern Upper Primary: The Class 6 to 8 level exam will have a total of 150 questions, and all questions will be compulsory. Subject-wise distribution of questions Subject-based options For Mathematics/Science Teacher: 60 questions from Mathematics and Science (60 marks) For Social Science Teacher: 60 questions from Social Studies (60 marks) For candidates of other subjects: One must choose either Mathematics/Science or Social Studies (60 questions) Primary School: For classes 1 to 5, all questions in the UP TET exam will be compulsory, and a total of 150 questions will be asked. Subject-wise Pattern The fee for General/OBC is 1000 rupees, SC-ST get relief General / EWS / Other Backwards Class (OBC) Paper-1: 1000 Paper-2: 1000 Scheduled Caste (SC) / Scheduled Tribe (ST) Paper-1: 500 Paper-2: 500 Persons with Disabilities Category Paper-1: 300 Paper-2: 300

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:President Murmu meets Mathura’s Premanand Maharaj; Mamata Banerjee releases TMC's manifesto ahead of polls more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. Gas shortages hit migrant labourers in Gujarat The impact of the ongoing war in the Middle East has started showing in India. In Gujarat, due to a shortage of cooking gas, street food stalls and small hotels eateries are closing down, leaving the traders unemployed. Additionally, labourers from UP-Bihar and thousands of students are forced to return home in this crisis. 2. President Murmu meets Premanand Maharaj in Mathura, holds spiritual discussion with family Mathura: President Droupadi Murmu met Premanand Maharaj at his ashram, holding a 25-minute spiritual discussion with family. She arrived amid rain and was warmly welcomed. On her Uttar Pradesh visit, she also visited Ayodhya, ISKCON and Prem Mandir, and is scheduled to visit Neem Karoli Baba’s ashram. 3. Ganga Iftar row: SP, Congress support questioned; experts cite Muslim vote bank politics Fourteen youths were arrested for holding an Iftar on the Ganga, sparking political row. SP and Congress questioned police action, while clerics and Hindu leaders criticised the act. Experts linked political support to vote bank considerations. Court sent accused to 14-day judicial custody after bail rejection. 4. SC dismisses PIL against Vantara, upholds SIT findings The Supreme Court dismissed a foundation's petition filed against Vantara. The court said that there was no violation of any domestic and international laws in Vantara. This petition against Vantara was filed by a foundation named Karunartham Viram. 5. UPSC returns UP DGP proposal, state given three months to resubmit plan Uttar Pradesh’s proposal to appoint a permanent DGP has been returned by UPSC citing discrepancies, with three months given to resubmit. Rajeev Krishna was leading earlier. Renuka Mishra and Alok Sharma were excluded, while the state continues without a full-time DGP since 2022. 6. UP CMO manager held in bribery trap, caught taking ₹2 lakh in Mahoba In Mahoba, a Health Department logistics manager was caught taking ₹2 lakh bribe in a vigilance trap after demanding ₹3.5 lakh from an employee. Arrested from a hotel, he pleaded for release. A case was registered under the Prevention of Corruption Act, and further investigation is underway. 7. OMCs increase premium grade petrol prices by over ₹2/litre Oil companies have increased the prices of premium petrol, such as Speed and Power, by ₹2.09-₹2.35 per litre on Friday. This increase is due to the rise in crude oil prices caused by the US-Israel and Iran war. Premium petrol is sold under the names Speed by BPCL, Power by HPCL, and XP95 by IOCL. 8. BSc student shot dead in Varanasi, four shots fired, accused flees scene A BSc student was shot dead on a college campus after four rounds were fired in broad daylight. The accused fled after discarding the pistol. The victim was declared dead at hospital. Protests turned violent, prompting heavy police deployment; investigation into motive is underway. 9. Bangkok return youth found dead nude in Gorakhpur, family alleges murder A 28-year-old man’s nude body was found on a toilet roof, with clothes hanging nearby. Family alleges murder, citing suspicious circumstances. Police said post-mortem will determine cause, with no formal complaint yet. The victim had recently returned from Bangkok for his sister’s wedding. 10. Mamata Banerjee releases TMC's manifesto ahead of polls Mamata Banerjee, Chief Minister of West Bengal and head of the All India Trinamool Congress (TMC), released the party’s manifesto for the state Assembly elections in Kolkata on Friday.

stories.title: ‘How is Atiq shown linked to ISI in Dhurandhar’:Former UP MP angry, Imran Masood calls it a rubbish film
stories.summary: Controversy has erupted in UP over actor Ranveer Singh's film 'Dhurandhar: The Revenge', depicting Atiq Ahmed's character and demonetization as a masterstroke. Congress MP Imran Masood from Saharanpur called the film nonsense. He said, "Who will watch this film and who will believe it? Former SP MP ST Hasan said, "Intelligence agencies and the police have not yet revealed whether Atiq had any connection with the Pakistani intelligence agency ISI. In such a situation, what is shown in the film has no basis." Meanwhile, AIMIM leader Waris Pathan said that just like 'Kerala Story-1 and 2', Muslims have also been targeted in Dhurandhar. Films that spread hatred in society should be immediately banned. Now read, who said what- Imran Masood said - Demonetisation was not a masterstroke Imran Masood said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi had broken the back of the country's economy by demonetisation, whereas in the film it has been shown as a masterstroke. Demonetisation was not a masterstroke, but a decision that harmed the country. He said that the decisions Rahul Gandhi had criticized are proving to be correct today. If glorification is to be done in films, then former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi should be shown and it should be told how she responded to US President Richard Nixon. Imran Masood stated that the government has run out of development issues, which is why politics of spreading hatred in society is being pursued. He questioned how long people would continue to be divided in the name of Hindu-Muslim. He alleged that Prime Minister Modi stands with folded hands before former US President Donald Trump to protect industrialists. ST Hasan said - Now films are being made for politics ST Hasan said that talks of Don Dawood Ibrahim's connection with ISI have been heard, but in the case of Atiq Ahmed, no Indian investigation agency has made any such revelation so far. An attempt is being made to run the film by creating controversy. He said - Today films are being made for politics. No positive message is being given to society. I think filmmakers take money from parties to spread hatred. Such films are being made to break the Hindu-Muslim fabric. Rajeev Rai said - Such films come only during elections SP MP from Ghosi, Rajeev Rai said - When it happened, he was not in our party, first thing. Secondly, the Bharatiya Janata Party has a propaganda machine, there is an advisor who keeps making movies about himself. He keeps making movies about his imaginary world. He can say anything to anyone, he can add any link. I would request him to make a movie where a brave person is shown apologizing, begging, taking a pension. Where the real character is shown informing. Where it is shown how in 1942 you were writing letters for the British with the Muslim League. This is the real truth, which is factually recorded in history. MP Rajeev Rai said - He has not seen the film, but whenever elections come, such films are deliberately released to influence the atmosphere. He alleged that the government indirectly supports such films. He also gave examples of films like 'Kashmir Files'. Maulana Shahabuddin Razvi said - The aim is to earn money by inciting controversy Maulana Shahabuddin Razvi Bareilvi, president of All India Muslim Jamaat, expressed displeasure over the film 'Dhurandhar 2'. He said - People in the film industry choose such subjects to earn money, which create controversy in society. That's why they add a Hindu-Muslim angle. Maulana Razvi said that their only aim now is to earn money, whereas earlier films were made to give a message to society, bring change and reform. Earlier, a film was made on 'Sambhal', and similarly, films like 'Udaipur Files', 'Kerala Story' and 'Pandit Ghuskhore' were also made in the same way. Why did the controversy arise? Actually, the film depicts the demonetization that took place in 2016. It also features a character 'Atif Ahmed' based on mafia don Atiq Ahmed. This character is played by Salim Siddiqui. Atif Ahmed's look, physique, mustache, and style are shown to be exactly similar to Atiq Ahmed. In the film, the character Atif Ahmed's connection with Pakistan's intelligence agency ISI is shown. He is depicted operating his entire criminal network even while being in jail. There is a dialogue in the film, "As long as Atif Ahmed is there, whether in jail or out... he will manage everything." According to the film, before the 2017 UP assembly elections, a large consignment of fake notes was to be brought to India from Pakistan through hawala. This character was given the responsibility of distributing money in the state, but the government gets wind of it. After this, demonetization is announced, and the entire plan is foiled. The film also features a scene of a mafia assassination. Additionally, a character based on former DGP Prashant Kumar has also been included. It shows the character, who has become the NSA, showing him Atiq's criminal profile.

stories.title: यूपी को 4 साल बाद मिलेगा स्थायी DGP, इस IPS अधिकारी का नाम सबसे आगे
stories.summary: UP New Permanent DGP: उत्तर प्रदेश को चार साल बाद स्थायी पुलिस महानिदेशक (DGP) मिलने वाला है। अभी तक राज्य में केवल कार्यवाहक DGP ही रहते आए हैं। अब योगी सरकार ने इस दिशा में कदम बढ़ा दिया है। राज्य सरकार ने केंद्र को जो प्रस्ताव भेजा है, उसमें IPS अधिकारी राजीव कृष्ण का नाम दूसरे स्थान पर है। संकेत मिल रहे हैं कि 1 अप्रैल से पहले ही उनका स्थायी DGP बनने का आदेश जारी हो सकता है। राजीव कृष्ण को 31 मई 2025 को कार्यवाहक DGP बनाया गया था। उन्होंने पूर्व DGP प्रशांत कुमार की जगह ली थी। वे उत्तर प्रदेश के लगातार पांचवें कार्यवाहक DGP हैं। इतने लंबे समय तक कोई स्थायी DGP न होने से कई सवाल उठते रहे हैं। अब राजीव कृष्ण को ही इस कुर्सी पर स्थायी रूप से बैठाया जा रहा है।

stories.title: Weather worsens in UP, hail hits Lucknow-Ayodhya:Heavy rain in 25 districts, storm in Kashi; 5 killed by lightning
stories.summary: The weather in UP has deteriorated. In Lucknow, sudden darkness enveloped at 10 AM on Friday. It rained with strong winds. Hail also fell in some areas. Ayodhya, Barabanki, Sitapur, and Siddharthnagar also experienced heavy rain with hail. Earlier, heavy rain occurred in Prayagraj and Mathura. A dust storm blew. Roads were waterlogged in many places. School children and people heading to offices were seen with raincoats and umbrellas. Intermittent rain occurred in more than 25 districts including Kanpur, Noida, Agra, Aligarh, and Meerut. In Kashi, there was a drizzle with a storm. People who set up shops on the ghats packed their belongings and returned. Meanwhile, 5 people, including 3 farmers, died due to lightning strikes in Prayagraj, Balrampur, Bahraich, and Mirzapur. Standing wheat crops fell in many places. Farmers say that unseasonal rain poses a threat of damage to mustard and potato crops as well. The Meteorological Department says that due to the activation of the Western Disturbance, the weather has changed across the entire state. The weather will remain bad for the next 2 days. Winds will blow at a speed of 40 km/h. Lucknow meteorologist Atul Singh said- Due to the Western Disturbance, there is a possibility of rain across the entire state. Its effect will start to decrease after 2 days. In the last 24 hours, winds blew at the fastest speed of 87 km/h in Mathura. The wind speed was recorded at 59 km/h in Noida, and 57 km/h in Agra and Bulandshahr. The highest rainfall was recorded in Baghpat and Bulandshahr, about 6 mm. Weather Pictures-

stories.title: Female patient raped at Saifai medical college:Staff member arrested, department head removed
stories.summary: A 40-year-old female patient was allegedly raped at Saifai Medical College in Etawah. She is mentally ill and had been admitted for nine months. The incident came to light during a routine medical examination, when she was found to be five months pregnant. The case caused a stir within the medical college. Prof. AK Mishra, Head of the Psychiatry Department, filed an FIR at Saifai police station on 18 March. Following preliminary investigation, police arrested cleaner Ravindra Kumar on 19 March. Administrative action taken by college The college management removed AK Mishra from his post. All staff of the psychiatry department were transferred to other departments. A three-member inquiry committee has been formed, and the administration has sought a report within 48 hours. A separate medical team has also been set up to monitor the condition of the victim. Police statement on the case Saifai CO Ramgopal Sharma said the victim has no family member present and had been admitted to the medical college on 24 June 2025, where she remained since. He said- ‘A sanitation worker sexually assaulted her. The accused has been arrested. CCTV footage has been sought from the medical college. Other ward staff and doctors are being questioned Accused employed through outsourcing University spokesperson Shivam Jha said Dr Arun Kumar Mishra informed the management about the matter through a letter on 18 March 2026. The allegation was against a sanitation worker employed through outsourcing. The matter was immediately handed over to the police. The management also took action against Dr Mishra, citing departmental negligence, and assigned additional charge to the Dean of Medicine. Inquiry committee and medical team formed Shivam Jha stated that a three-member inquiry committee was constituted on 19 March to ensure justice for the victim. The panel will investigate the role of department staff, security arrangements and any negligence. At the same time, considering the patient’s condition, the Chief Medical Superintendent formed a special medical team under the Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology. The team will oversee all necessary tests and treatment related to the woman’s pregnancy and overall health. Report sought from authorities Information about the case was sent to the District Magistrate of Etawah on 19 March. A report has also been sought from the Internal Complaints Committee. The matter is being treated seriously at the administrative level and is under continuous monitoring. Police raise key questions Police are examining the possible involvement of other staff and officials and are seeking answers to several questions-

stories.title: Ganga Iftar row—Why SP and Congress are in support ?:Experts cite Muslim vote bank; Maulana says, 'throwing bones is wrong'
stories.summary: Fourteen young men in Varanasi organised a Roza Iftar party on a boat in the Ganga river, filmed a reel and shared it on social media. The video showed them eating biryani. Following a complaint by the BJP Yuva Morcha, police arrested all 14 and sent them to jail. The incident has since triggered a political controversy. Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav and Congress leader Imran Pratapgarhi supported the youths, questioning police action. Meanwhile, Muslim clerics from Bareilly, Varanasi and Saharanpur criticised the act, calling it inappropriate and against Islamic principles. Religious leaders criticise the act Maulana: Throwing bones into Ganga is wrong Maulana Shahabuddin Razvi Bareilvi, President of the All India Muslim Jamaat, said Islam promotes simplicity and discourages showmanship. He stated that charity and good deeds should be done discreetly. 'These boys lack understanding of Deen (religion),' he said. 'They held Iftar on the Ganga and allegedly threw bones into the river after eating biryani. This is completely wrong and unacceptable.' He added that such actions harm the sanctity of the Ganga and criticised political leaders supporting the act, saying they should seek guidance from religious scholars. Varanasi cleric: No place for such acts in Islam SM Yasin, Joint Secretary of Anjuman Intezamia Masajid in Varanasi, said Iftar is a purely religious act, not a picnic or outing. He stressed that Maghrib prayers are obligatory after Iftar. 'What have their families taught them?' he asked. ‘Such actions only bring disrepute to Islam.’ Alternate view: Police acted under pressure Maulana Sufiyan Nizami, spokesperson for Firangi Mahal, offered a contrasting view. He argued that the police acted under public pressure. 'In Varanasi, people consume alcohol on cruises, yet no action is taken because there is no protest,' he said. 'I am not in favour of filing an FIR. The police acted under pressure, which is not appropriate under the law.' He also referred to a previous controversy in Sambhal, alleging misuse of authority. Hindu religious leader reacts Ram Ratan Giri, secretary of Panchayati Akhara Shri Niranjani, condemned the incident, emphasising the sacred status of the Ganga. ‘We consider the Ganga as a mother. Is it now a place for Iftar parties? Should bones be thrown into it?’ he said. He also questioned why SP and Congress were supporting the youths, stating that political backing of such actions sends the wrong message. Political reactions intensify debate Akhilesh Yadav questions police action SP chief Akhilesh Yadav alleged that the arrests were made to appease the government and create divisions. He pointed out that luxury cruise ships operating in Varanasi serve alcohol and discharge waste into the Ganga, asking what action had been taken against them. Imran Pratapgarhi slams police Congress Rajya Sabha MP Imran Pratapgarhi said the arrests were triggered by the objections of a 'small-time leader'. 'A group of youths was having Iftar on a boat when someone’s sentiments were hurt, leading to arrests,' he said. He accused Uttar Pradesh Police of being quick to act against Muslims while ignoring similar issues involving others. Expert views: Vote bank politics at play Call for collective criticism Senior journalist Samiratmaj Mishra said the facts, such as whether bones were actually thrown, should be established through investigation. However, he noted that holding an Iftar party on the Ganga would not be widely considered appropriate. 'Ganga is a symbol of religious faith. Political parties should have collectively criticised the act,' he said, adding that comparisons with sewage discharge or cruises are misplaced. ‘Appeasement Politics’ alleged Veteran journalist Alok Pathak described the political support as an example of 'Muslim appeasement'. He argued that when religious leaders themselves oppose the act, political backing becomes difficult to justify. He also maintained that pollution from sewage and deliberate disposal of food waste cannot be equated. Vote Bank considerations Senior journalist Harshvardhan said the reactions reflect electoral calculations. He argued that political parties aim to retain Muslim support, fearing voter shifts. According to him, both SP and Congress seek to consolidate Muslim votes, with leaders like Rahul Gandhi and Akhilesh Yadav viewing the community as a crucial electoral base. He added that while environmental concerns about the Ganga are widely acknowledged, actions perceived as disrespectful to religious sentiments draw sharper reactions. How the incident unfolded ? The incident took place in the Tadtalla area of Madanpura in Varanasi. Fourteen youths from the Babu Bidi family planned an Iftar party on the Ganga on 16 March. They boarded a boat at Assi Ghat, which travelled to Namo Ghat. During the gathering, they recorded a reel showing themselves eating chicken biryani and posted it on Instagram. The video sparked controversy. BJP Yuva Morcha metropolitan president Rajat Jaiswal filed a police complaint, alleging that the youths threw chicken bones into the river after eating. A case was registered at Kotwali police station, and all 14 were arrested. Court proceedings and jail The accused were presented in court at around 8 pm on 19 March. Kashi Police told the Chief Judicial Magistrate (CJM) court that the youths had effectively hijacked the boat and coerced the boatman to conduct the Iftar on the river. They also cited the making and sharing of videos as evidence of deliberate conduct. The families filed bail applications, but the court rejected all pleas. The youths have been remanded to 14 days in judicial custody, with the next bail hearing scheduled for 1 April. During the hearing, five of the accused reportedly broke down in court. With their custody extending through the festive period, they are set to spend Eid in jail.

stories.title: BSc student shot dead in Varanasi:4 shots fired; accused threw pistol in garbage and fled
stories.summary: A BSc student was shot dead in broad daylight inside the campus of Uday Pratap College in Varanasi. The attacker fired four rounds at the student outside a classroom, causing him to collapse in a pool of blood. A friend of the victim said they rushed to the spot after hearing the gunshots. The accused allegedly pointed a pistol at them as well before fleeing. He is said to have discarded the weapon in a heap of rubbish while escaping. Victim taken to hospital, declared dead Following the incident, chaos gripped the college. Teachers and students gathered at the scene as the injured student was rushed to the BHU Trauma Centre. Doctors there declared him dead on arrival. The shooting took place on Friday afternoon outside the Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences. Violence and vandalism on campus After the killing, students staged protests that quickly turned violent. Acts of vandalism were reported within the campus, and shops outside the college were also targeted. Police responded by shutting the college gates and ordering the closure of more than 150 shops in the surrounding area. A heavy police deployment, including personnel from seven police stations, has been stationed inside the campus to maintain order. Victim and accused identified The deceased has been identified as 23-year-old Surya Pratap Singh, a resident of Ghazipur. The accused, Manjeet, is a second-year BA student reportedly from the Chandmari area of Varanasi. The reason behind the attack remains unknown, and police investigations are ongoing. See 4 pictures-

stories.title: Bangkok return man's nude body found on terrace in Gorakhpur:Clothes found hanging 25 metres away on tree; mother alleges murder, demands probe
stories.summary: A 28-year-old man’s nude body was discovered on the roof of a toilet in Gorakhpur. His jeans and T-shirt were found hanging from a tree 25 metres away. His mother alleges murder and demands that those responsible be hanged. According to police, Rishabh Yadav worked in Bangkok, the capital of Thailand. He had returned home on 19 February for his sister’s wedding. His body was found on Thursday morning. A condom was in his hand, and there were scratch marks on his stomach. No other injury marks were found. The incident occurred within the Gagaha police station area. SSP Dr Kaustubh said- The post-mortem will be conducted today. Further action will follow based on the report. No written complaint has been filed by the family so far.’ Family’s reaction and discovery of body Rishabh’s father, Rajendra Yadav, runs a flour mill 20 metres from the Gorakhpur–Varanasi highway. On Thursday morning, he reached the mill and saw a body on the roof of the toilet behind it. He informed the police, who arrived with a forensic team. The body was sent to BRD Medical College. On receiving the news, the mother and wife rushed to the scene. The mother fainted while crying. His wife said tearfully, 'My husband was murdered and his body was dumped. Strict action must be taken against those responsible.' Family background Rishabh was from Rawatpar and worked in Bangkok with his father, Uday Chand Yadav. He married Chandni seven years ago and had two sons, aged six years and two-and-a-half years. He had two brothers and two sisters. His mother, Guddi Devi, said he had come from Bangkok for his younger sister’s wedding on 19 February. Ten days after the wedding, his father returned to Bangkok, but Rishabh remained in Gorakhpur.

stories.title: President Murmu meets Premanand Maharaj in Mathura:Arrives with family at ashram, holds 25-min spiritual discussion
stories.summary: President Droupadi Murmu met Premanand Maharaj in Mathura, where they held a spiritual discussion for 25 minutes. The President arrived at Premanandji’s ashram with her family at 7 am on Friday amid rain and greeted him with folded hands. Premanandji responded with ‘Radhe-Radhe’. The President was welcomed by ashram volunteers with garlands and a ceremonial scarf. She also wished him on his birthday, which was on Thursday. 3-day Uttar Pradesh visit The President is on a three-day visit to Uttar Pradesh. On the second day, she is scheduled to visit the ashram of Neem Karoli Baba and offer prayers to Hanuman ji. She will then visit the Ramakrishna Mission Hospital to inaugurate Western Uttar Pradesh’s most modern cancer unit. This is her second visit to Mathura; she had previously visited on 25 September last year. See 3 pictures- Warm reception at Ashram The President was received by the ashram’s attendants with garlands and stoles. Chairs were arranged for her and her family at Kelikunj Ashram. She was accompanied by her daughter Itishree Murmu, son-in-law Ganesh Hembram, and granddaughters Adyashree and Nityashree. Emotional spiritual interaction During the spiritual discussion with Premanand Maharaj, the President reportedly became emotional. The interaction took place privately inside a hut, attended only by the President, her family, and Premanand’s close disciples. Visit to Ayodhya and Ram Temple On the first day of her visit, the President offered prayers to Ramlala in Ayodhya. She installed the Ram Yantra in the Ram Darbar on the second floor and toured the temple complex. Yogi Adityanath briefed her on the ongoing construction work related to the temple. The President said that Lord Shri Ram was born in Ayodhya and described it as a matter of great fortune to set foot on the sacred land. ISKCON and Prem Mandir visits In the evening, she travelled from Ayodhya to Mathura and visited the ISKCON temple, where she offered prayers to Radha-Shyam Sundar. She praised the temple’s decoration and interacted with children, distributing chocolates. After spending about half an hour at ISKCON, she proceeded to Prem Mandir to offer prayers.

stories.title: CMO office manager held in bribery trap in UP:Vigilance raid catches official taking ₹2 lakh in Mahoba; breaks down during arrest
stories.summary: In Mahoba, a vigilance team dragged away the Health Department’s Family Planning Logistic Manager. He had demanded a bribe of ₹3.5 lakh from a contractual employee. Yesterday he had called the employee to a hotel to take the first instalment of ₹2 lakh, where he was caught red-handed. He broke down in tears and kept shaking his hands and legs in an attempt to free himself. The man apologised to the vigilance officers and pleaded, “Sir, I fold my hands, please let me go.” The officers detained him forcefully and said, “Take him away. Put him in the vehicle.” The manager tried with all his strength to escape from the team’s grip. One team member held his belt while another dragged him towards the Bolero vehicle. See 3 pictures... Now read the complete sequence of events... Allegation - CMO had asked to meet the manager Meraj Mohammad from Hamirpur is an account manager at Panwadi Community Health Center in Mahoba. He said, “I had asked the Chief Medical Officer (CMO) for transfer or adjustment to Kabrai Community Health Center. The CMO said, go meet Jitesh. Jitesh is the Family Planning Logistics Manager. He is also a contract employee and has a clerk-like position”. He added, “When I met Jitesh, he said, give ₹3.5 lakh, your work will be done. I complained about this to the Jhansi Vigilance officers. Vigilance planned to catch accused Jitesh red-handed”. Manager called employee to hotel basement He added, “On Thursday, I called Jitesh and said the money has been arranged. Where should I give it? To this, Jitesh called me to a hotel basement about 5 km away from the CMO office”. After reaching the hotel, as soon as he gave ₹2 lakh to the manager, the team deployed in plain clothes caught him on the spot. When the accused's hands were washed, they turned pink due to the effect of the chemical, confirming the acceptance of the bribe. After arrest, the accused was brought to the city police station. Where he is being intensively interrogated in a closed room. In this case, CMO Asaram has given clarification. He said, “Meraj's allegations are baseless. Meraj was pressuring me to forcefully transfer him”. He added, “I have not had any conversation with Meraj for the past one and a half years. He had come to my residence and misbehaved. Since then I have not talked to him. He was transferred only due to irregularities found in his work. The person from whom Meraj is alleging to have demanded a bribe, his work is related to logistics.” Vigilance team in-charge said - Preparing to send accused to jail Meanwhile, Vigilance team in-charge Piyush Pandey said, “A case has been registered against the accused under the Prevention of Corruption Act. Preparations are being made to send him to jail. Investigation is also being done about who else could be involved in this case”.

stories.title: UP permanent DGP proposal returned by UPSC:3 months to resubmit; Rajeev Krishna topped in earlier list
stories.summary: The proposal for appointing a permanent DGP in Uttar Pradesh has been stalled for now. The UPSC has raised objections and returned the proposal to the Chief Secretary. The Commission said a fresh proposal should be prepared in line with the 2025 guidelines and Supreme Court rulings, and resubmitted. A three-month window has been given for this. In the earlier proposal, Rajeev Krishna was widely expected to be appointed as the permanent DGP. He was made acting DGP of Uttar Pradesh on 31 May 2025, replacing Prashant Kumar. He is the fifth consecutive acting DGP in the state. Renuka Mishra removed from the race Senior IPS officer Renuka Mishra, once a strong contender, has been excluded from the DGP race. The Uttar Pradesh government held her responsible for lapses linked to the 2024 police recruitment paper leak. Mishra served as Chairperson of the Uttar Pradesh Police Recruitment and Promotion Board from 14 February 2023 to 5 March 2024. During her tenure, the constable recruitment examination paper was leaked on 24 February, leading to the cancellation of the test. Investigations revealed that a blacklisted firm had been entrusted with printing the question papers. Following this, Mishra was removed from her position and placed on a waiting list. In its communication to the UPSC, the state government stated that the irregularities rendered her unsuitable for appointment as DGP. Why was Alok Sharma not considered ? The state government also excluded Alok Sharma, currently serving in the Special Protection Group on central deputation. Sources indicate that 5 February 2026 was treated as the official vacancy date for the DGP post, following a directive from the Supreme Court to appoint a permanent DGP. As per UPSC norms, only officers with at least six months of remaining service are eligible. Sharma’s remaining tenure falls short of this requirement, leading to his exclusion. Likely panel for DGP appointment With Mishra and Sharma out of contention, the panel expected to be considered by the UPSC includes- Additionally, the state has forwarded a broader list of officers up to the 1994 batch. These include Ashutosh Pandey and Anand Swaroop (1992 batch); Sanjay Singhal, SB Shiradkar, Zaki Ahmed, KS Pratap Kumar, Rajiv Sabharwal and Vitul Kumar (1993 batch); and BK Singh, Akhil Kumar, Raja Srivastava, DK Thakur, Sujit Pandey, Prakash D and Jai Narayan Singh (1994 batch). Proposal returned by UPSC A proposal for appointing the permanent DGP, sent by Chief Secretary SP Goyal, was returned by the UPSC due to technical discrepancies. The primary issue was that the proposal had been submitted in an outdated format rather than the revised one mandated by the आयोग. 4 years without a permanent DGP Uttar Pradesh has not had a full-time DGP since Mukul Goel was removed on 11 May 2022. Since then, a series of acting DGPs have held the position- Krishna, a 1991 batch IPS officer, is currently set to serve until June 2029. A Technocrat image and policing innovations Rajiv Krishna is regarded as a technocrat within the police force. As Additional Director General (ADG), he developed the ‘Operation Pehchan’ application, aimed at tracking criminals. He also integrated digital monitoring systems for the Women Beat programme and Anti-Romeo Squads. His initiatives include the introduction of e-Malkhana (digital evidence storage), digitisation of case records and focused campaigns against cybercrime. During his tenure as Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) in Agra, he led effective operations against kidnapping gangs operating in ravine areas. Career trajectory and postings After joining the IPS in 1991, Krishna began his career as a trainee in Allahabad (now Prayagraj). He later served as Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP) in Bareilly, Kanpur and Aligarh. On 10 March 1997, he became Superintendent of Police (SP) of Firozabad. He subsequently served as SSP in multiple districts, including Etawah, Mathura, Fatehgarh, Bulandshahr, Gautam Buddh Nagar, Agra, Lucknow and Bareilly. During administrative restructuring under Mayawati’s government, he was appointed DIG of Lucknow. He later served as IG of Meerut Range and went on central deputation in 2012, returning in 2017. Strong family background in public service Krishna comes from a family with a long-standing presence in civil services and politics. His wife, Meenakshi Singh, serves as Deputy Secretary in the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) in Noida. His brother-in-law, Rajeshwar Singh, is currently an MLA from Sarojini Nagar in Lucknow and a former IPS officer who later joined the Enforcement Directorate. Rajeshwar’s wife, Lakshmi Singh, is the Police Commissioner of Gautam Buddh Nagar. Krishna’s father-in-law also served as a Deputy Inspector General of Police. With the administrative process nearing completion, Uttar Pradesh appears set to end its prolonged reliance on acting DGPs, marking a significant shift in its policing leadership structure.
